verses.1:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai, in the tabernacle of the covenant, on the first day of the second month, in the second year of their departure from Egypt, saying,
verses.1:2: "Take the total of the entire congregation of the sons of Israel by their clans and houses, and the names of each one, everyone of the male sex
verses.1:3: from twenty years old and above, of all the strong men from Israel, and you shall count them by their companies, you and Aaron.
verses.1:4: And there shall be with you the leaders of the tribes and of the houses in their clans,
verses.1:5: whose names are these: from Reuben, Elizur, son of Shedeur;
verses.1:6: from Simeon, Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai;
verses.1:7: from Judah, Nahshon, son of Amminadab;
verses.1:8: from Issachar, Nethanel, son of Zuar;
verses.1:9: from Zebulun, Eliab, son of Helon;
verses.1:10: and of the sons of Joseph, from Ephraim, Elishama, son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur;
verses.1:11: from Benjamin, Abidan, son of Gideon;
verses.1:12: from Dan, Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai;
verses.1:13: from Asher, Pagiel, son of Ochran;
verses.1:14: from Gad, Eliasaph, son of Deuel;
verses.1:15: from Naphtali, Ahira, son of Enan."
verses.1:16: These were the most noble leaders of the multitude by their tribes and clans, and the heads of the army of Israel,
verses.1:17: whom Moses and Aaron took with the entire multitude of the common people,
verses.1:18: and they assembled them on the first day of the second month, registering them by clans, houses, families, heads, and the names of each one from twenty years old and above,
verses.1:19: just as the Lord had commanded Moses. And they were counted in the desert of Sinai.
verses.1:20: From Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, by their generations and families and houses, and the names of the individual heads, everyone of the male sex from twenty years old and above, going out to war:
verses.1:22: From the sons of Simeon, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names and heads of each one, everyone of the male sex from twenty years old and above, going out to war:
verses.1:24: From the sons of Gad, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who would go out to war:
verses.1:26: From the sons of Judah, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war,
verses.1:27: there were registered seventy-four thousand six hundred.
verses.1:28: From the sons of Issachar, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who would go out to war,
verses.1:29: there were registered fifty-four thousand four hundred.
verses.1:30: From the sons of Zebulun, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:32: From the sons of Joseph, of the sons of Ephraim, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:34: Now of the sons of Manasseh, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:36: From the sons of Benjamin, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:38: From the sons of Dan, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:40: From the sons of Asher, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:42: From the sons of Naphtali, by their generations and families and the houses of their clans, there were registered by the names of each one from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go out to war:
verses.1:44: These are the ones whom Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel counted, each one by the houses of their clans.
verses.1:45: And the entire number of the sons of Israel by their houses and families, from twenty years old and above, who were able to go out to war, was
verses.1:46: six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
verses.1:47: The Levites, however, were not counted with them in the tribe of their families.
verses.1:48: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.1:49: "Do not count the tribe of Levi, nor shall you place their total with the sons of Israel,
verses.1:50: but appoint them over the tabernacle of the testimony and all its vessels, and whatever pertains to the ceremonies. They themselves shall carry the tabernacle and all its utensils, and they shall be in service, and they shall camp around the tabernacle.
verses.1:51: When setting out, the Levites shall take down the tabernacle; when pitching camp, they shall set it up. Any outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
verses.1:52: Now the sons of Israel shall pitch camp, each one by his companies and formations and army.
verses.1:53: But the Levites shall pitch tents around the tabernacle, so that indignation may not come upon the multitude of the sons of Israel, and they shall keep watch in the guard duties of the tabernacle of the testimony."
verses.1:54: Therefore the sons of Israel did according to everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.2:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.2:2: "The sons of Israel will camp, each by companies, standards, and banners, and by the houses of their kindred, all around the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.2:3: Toward the east, Judah will pitch tents by the companies of his army, and the leader of his sons will be Nahshon son of Amminadab.
verses.2:4: And the entire total of warriors from his lineage was seventy-four thousand six hundred.
verses.2:5: Next to him camped those of the tribe of Issachar, whose leader was Nethanel son of Zuar.
verses.2:6: And the entire number of his warriors was fifty-four thousand four hundred.
verses.2:7: In the tribe of Zebulun, the leader was Eliab son of Helon.
verses.2:8: The entire army of warriors from his lineage was fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
verses.2:9: All who were enumerated in the camp of Judah were one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred; and by their companies they will go out first.
verses.2:10: In the camp of the sons of Reuben toward the southern region, the leader will be Elizur son of Shedeur.
verses.2:11: And the whole army of his warriors who were counted was forty-six thousand five hundred.
verses.2:12: Next to him camped those of the tribe of Simeon, whose leader was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
verses.2:13: And the whole army of his warriors who were counted was fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
verses.2:14: In the tribe of Gad, the leader was Eliasaph son of Deuel.
verses.2:15: And the whole army of his warriors who were counted was forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
verses.2:16: All who were mustered in the camp of Reuben were one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty by their companies; they will set out in the second place.
verses.2:17: Then the tabernacle of the testimony will be lifted up through the services of the Levites and their companies; just as it will be erected, so also it will be taken down. Each will set out by their places and ranks.
verses.2:18: Toward the western region will be the camp of the sons of Ephraim, whose leader was Elishama son of Ammihud.
verses.2:19: The whole army of his warriors who were counted was forty thousand five hundred.
verses.2:20: And with them will be the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, whose leader was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
verses.2:21: And the whole army of his warriors who were counted was thirty-two thousand two hundred.
verses.2:22: In the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, the leader was Abidan son of Gideon.
verses.2:23: And the whole army of his warriors who were mustered was thirty-five thousand four hundred.
verses.2:24: All who were counted in the camp of Ephraim were one hundred eight thousand one hundred by their companies; they will set out third.
verses.2:25: Toward the northern side camped the sons of Dan, whose leader was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
verses.2:26: The whole army of his warriors who were counted was sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
verses.2:27: Next to him, those of the tribe of Asher pitched tents; their leader was Pagiel son of Ochran.
verses.2:28: The whole army of his warriors who were counted was forty-one thousand five hundred.
verses.2:29: Of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, the leader was Ahira son of Enan.
verses.2:30: The whole army of his warriors was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
verses.2:31: All who were counted in the camp of Dan were one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred; and they will set out last."
verses.2:32: This is the number of the sons of Israel, by the houses of their kindred and the companies of the divided army: six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
verses.2:33: The Levites, however, were not counted among the sons of Israel, for so the Lord had directed Moses.
verses.2:34: And the sons of Israel did according to all that the Lord had commanded. They camped by their companies and set out by families and the houses of their fathers.
verses.3:1: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses on the day when the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
verses.3:2: And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: his firstborn Nadab, then Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.3:3: These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests who were anointed and whose hands were filled and consecrated so that they might exercise the priesthood.
verses.3:4: For Nadab and Abihu died when they offered foreign fire in the sight of the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, without children; and Eleazar and Ithamar exercised the priesthood before Aaron their father.
verses.3:5: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.3:6: "Bring near the tribe of Levi, and make them stand in the sight of Aaron the priest so that they may minister to him and keep watch,
verses.3:7: and observe whatever pertains to the service of the multitude before the tabernacle of the testimony,
verses.3:8: and guard the vessels of the tabernacle, serving in its ministry.
verses.3:9: And you will give the Levites as a gift
verses.3:10: to Aaron and his sons, to whom they have been handed over by the sons of Israel. But you will appoint Aaron and his sons over the service of the priesthood. An outsider who approaches to minister will die."
verses.3:11: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.3:12: "I have taken the Levites from the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the sons of Israel, and the Levites will be Mine.
verses.3:13: For every firstborn is Mine: from the time I struck the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself whatever is born first in Israel; from man even to livestock, they are Mine. I am the Lord."
verses.3:14: And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
verses.3:15: "Count the sons of Levi by the houses of their fathers and families, every male from one month and upward."
verses.3:16: Moses counted them, as the Lord had commanded,
verses.3:17: and the sons of Levi were found by their names: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari.
verses.3:18: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
verses.3:19: The sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
verses.3:20: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.
verses.3:21: From Gershon there were two families, the Libnite and the Shimeite,
verses.3:22: whose people of the male sex were counted from one month and upward, seven thousand five hundred.
verses.3:23: These will pitch camp behind the tabernacle toward the west,
verses.3:24: under the leader Eliasaph, son of Lael.
verses.3:25: And they will have the watch in the tabernacle of the covenant:
verses.3:26: the tabernacle itself and its covering, the hanging that is drawn before the doors of the shelter of the covenant, and the curtains of the courtyard; also the hanging that is suspended at the entrance of the courtyard of the tabernacle, and whatever pertains to the rite of the altar, the cords of the tabernacle, and all its utensils.
verses.3:27: The clan of Kohath will have the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite, and Uzzielite peoples. These are the families of the Kohathites, enrolled by their names.
verses.3:28: All of the male sex from one month and upward, eight thousand six hundred, will have the watch of the sanctuary,
verses.3:29: and will encamp on the southern side.
verses.3:30: And their leader will be Elizaphan, son of Uzziel,
verses.3:31: and they will guard the ark, and the table and the lampstand, the altars and the vessels of the sanctuary with which ministry is performed, and the veil, and all furnishings of this kind.
verses.3:32: Now the leader of the leaders of the Levites, Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, will be over the watchmen of the custody of the sanctuary.
verses.3:33: Now from Merari there will be the Mahlite and Mushite peoples, enrolled by their names:
verses.3:34: all of the male sex from one month and upward, six thousand two hundred.
verses.3:35: Their leader is Zuriel, son of Abihail; they will encamp on the northern side.
verses.3:36: Under their custody will be the boards of the tabernacle and the bars, and the pillars and their bases, and all things that pertain to service of this kind,
verses.3:37: and the pillars of the courtyard all around with their bases, and the pegs with the cords.
verses.3:38: Moses, and Aaron with his sons, will encamp before the tabernacle of the covenant, that is, on the eastern side, having custody of the sanctuary in the midst of the sons of Israel. Any stranger who approaches will die.
verses.3:39: All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the Lord by their families, of the male sex from one month and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
verses.3:40: And the Lord said to Moses, "Count the firstborn of the male sex from the sons of Israel from one month and upward, and you will have their sum.
verses.3:41: And you will take the Levites for Me in place of every firstborn of the sons of Israel; I am the Lord; and their livestock in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the sons of Israel."
verses.3:42: Moses enrolled the firstborn of the sons of Israel, just as the Lord had commanded,
verses.3:43: and the males by their names, from one month and upward, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
verses.3:44: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.3:45: "Take the Levites in place of the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock, and the Levites will be Mine. I am the Lord.
verses.3:46: Now as the price of the two hundred seventy-three who exceed the number of the Levites from the firstborn of the sons of Israel,
verses.3:47: you will receive five shekels for each head according to the measure of the sanctuary (a shekel has twenty obols),
verses.3:48: and you will give the money to Aaron and his sons, the price of those who are in excess."
verses.3:49: Therefore Moses took the money of those who had been in excess, and whom they had redeemed from the Levites,
verses.3:50: for the firstborn of the sons of Israel, one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary,
verses.3:51: and he gave it to Aaron and his sons according to the word that the Lord had commanded him.
verses.4:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.4:2: "Take the total of the sons of Kohath from the midst of the Levites, by their houses and families,
verses.4:3: from the thirtieth year and upward, up to the fiftieth year, of all who enter to stand and minister in the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.4:4: This is the service of the sons of Kohath: into the tabernacle of the covenant and the Holy of Holies
verses.4:5: Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp is to be moved, and they shall take down the veil that hangs before the doors, and wrap the ark of the testimony with it,
verses.4:6: and they shall cover it again with a covering of violet skins, and spread an entirely blue cloth over it, and insert the poles.
verses.4:7: They shall also wrap the table of presentation in a blue cloth, and place with it the censers and small mortars, the cups and bowls for pouring libations; the loaves shall always be on it;
verses.4:8: and they shall spread a scarlet cloth over it, which they shall cover again with a covering of violet skins, and insert the poles.
verses.4:9: They shall also take a blue cloth, with which they shall cover the lampstand with its lamps and tongs and snuffers, and all the oil vessels that are needed for preparing the lamps;
verses.4:10: and over everything they shall place a covering of violet skins, and insert the poles.
verses.4:11: Likewise, they shall wrap the golden altar in a blue cloth, and spread a covering of violet skins over it, and insert the poles.
verses.4:12: All the vessels with which ministry is performed in the sanctuary they shall wrap in a blue cloth, and spread a covering of violet skins over them, and insert the poles.
verses.4:13: Moreover, they shall clean the altar of ashes, and wrap it in a purple cloth,
verses.4:14: and place with it all the vessels that they use in its ministry, that is, the fire receptacles, the small forks and three-pronged forks, the hooks, and the shovels. All the vessels of the altar they shall cover together with a covering of violet skins, and insert the poles.
verses.4:15: And when Aaron and his sons have wrapped the sanctuary and all its vessels at the moving of the camp, then the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry the wrapped things; and they shall not touch the vessels of the sanctuary, so that they do not die. These are the burdens of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the covenant:
verses.4:16: over whom shall be Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to whose care belong the oil for preparing the lamps, and the compounded incense, and the sacrifice that is always offered, and the anointing oil, and whatever pertains to the service of the tabernacle and of all the vessels that are in the sanctuary."
verses.4:17: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.4:18: "Do not destroy the people of Kohath from the midst of the Levites,
verses.4:19: but do this for them, so that they may live and not die if they touch the most holy things. Aaron and his sons shall enter, and they themselves shall arrange the tasks of each one and apportion what each one is to carry.
verses.4:20: Others shall not look with any curiosity at the things that are in the sanctuary before they are wrapped; otherwise they will die."
verses.4:21: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.4:22: "Take the total of the sons of Gershon also, by their houses and families and clans,
verses.4:23: from thirty years and upward, up to fifty years. Count all who enter and minister in the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.4:24: This is the duty of the family of the Gershonites,
verses.4:25: to carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the roof of the covenant, the other covering, and over all the violet covering, and the tent-curtain that hangs at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant,
verses.4:26: the curtains of the courtyard, and the veil at the entrance that is before the tabernacle. All things that pertain to the altar, the cords, and the vessels of ministry,
verses.4:27: at the command of Aaron and his sons, the sons of Gershon shall carry; and each one shall know to what burden he must be assigned.
verses.4:28: This is the service of the family of the Gershonites in the tabernacle of the covenant, and they shall be under the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.4:29: You shall also register the sons of Merari by families and the houses of their fathers,
verses.4:30: from thirty years and upward, up to fifty years, all who enter for the duty of their ministry and the service of the covenant of the testimony.
verses.4:31: These are their burdens: they shall carry the boards of the tabernacle and its bars, the pillars and their bases,
verses.4:32: also the pillars of the courtyard all around with their bases and pegs and ropes. They shall receive all the vessels and equipment by number, and so they shall carry them.
verses.4:33: This is the duty of the family of the Merarites and the ministry in the tabernacle of the covenant, and they shall be under the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest."
verses.4:34: Therefore Moses and Aaron and the leaders of the assembly registered the sons of Kohath by clans and the houses of their fathers,
verses.4:35: from thirty years and upward, up to the fiftieth year, all who enter for the ministry of the tabernacle of the covenant;
verses.4:36: and there were found two thousand seven hundred fifty.
verses.4:37: This is the number of the people of Kohath who enter the tabernacle of the covenant; these Moses and Aaron counted according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.4:38: The sons of Gershon were also counted by clans and the houses of their fathers,
verses.4:39: from thirty years and upward, up to the fiftieth year, all who enter to minister in the tabernacle of the covenant;
verses.4:40: and there were found two thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.4:41: This is the people of the Gershonites, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the word of the Lord.
verses.4:42: The sons of Merari were also counted by clans and the houses of their fathers,
verses.4:43: from thirty years and upward, up to the fiftieth year, all who enter to fulfill the rites of the tabernacle of the covenant;
verses.4:44: and there were found three thousand two hundred.
verses.4:45: This is the number of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron registered according to the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.4:46: All who were registered from the Levites, and whom Moses and Aaron and the leaders of Israel caused to be registered by name, by clans and the houses of their fathers,
verses.4:47: from thirty years and upward, up to the fiftieth year, entering for the ministry of the tabernacle and for carrying the burdens,
verses.4:48: were altogether eight thousand five hundred eighty.
verses.4:49: According to the word of the Lord, Moses registered them, each one according to his duty and burdens, just as the Lord had commanded him.
verses.5:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.5:2: "Command the sons of Israel to expel from the camp every leper, and whoever has a discharge of seed, and whoever is defiled on account of a dead person;
verses.5:3: expel both male and female from the camp, so that they do not contaminate it while they dwell with you."
verses.5:4: And the sons of Israel did so, and expelled them outside the camp, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
verses.5:5: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.5:6: "Speak to the sons of Israel: A man or a woman, when they commit any of all the sins that commonly happen to people, and through negligence transgress the command of the Lord and commit an offense,
verses.5:7: they shall confess their sin, and they shall repay the principal amount itself, and a fifth part in addition, to the one against whom they have sinned.
verses.5:8: But if there is no one to receive it, they shall give it to the Lord, and it shall belong to the priest, apart from the ram that is offered for atonement, so that it may be an appeasing sacrifice.
verses.5:9: Also all the firstfruits that the sons of Israel offer belong to the priest;
verses.5:10: and whatever is offered into the sanctuary by each person, and is delivered into the hands of the priest, shall be his."
verses.5:11: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.5:12: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: A man whose wife has gone astray, and despising her husband
verses.5:13: has slept with another man, and the husband has not been able to detect this, but the adultery lies hidden and cannot be proved by witnesses, because she was not found in illicit intercourse:
verses.5:14: if a spirit of jealousy has stirred up the man against his wife, who either has been defiled or is assailed by a false suspicion:
verses.5:15: he shall bring her to the priest, and shall present an offering for her, a tenth part of a seah of barley flour; he shall not pour oil over it, nor place frankincense on it, because it is a sacrifice of jealousy, and an offering investigating adultery.
verses.5:16: Therefore the priest shall bring her forward and set her before the Lord,
verses.5:17: and he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and he shall put a small amount of earth from the floor of the tabernacle into it.
verses.5:18: And when the woman stands in the sight of the Lord, he shall uncover her head, and place upon her hands the sacrifice of remembrance and the offering of jealousy; he himself, however, shall hold the most bitter waters, in which he has gathered curses with imprecation.
verses.5:19: And he shall put her under oath and say, 'If no strange man has slept with you, and if you have not been defiled by abandoning the marriage bed of your husband, these most bitter waters, into which I have gathered curses, will not harm you.
verses.5:20: But if you have turned aside from your husband, and have been defiled, and have lain with another man,
verses.5:21: you will be subject to these curses: may the Lord make you a curse and an example to all among His people; may He make your thigh rot, and may your swelling womb burst apart.
verses.5:22: May the cursed waters enter into your belly, and as your womb swells, may your thigh rot.' And the woman shall answer, 'Amen, amen.'
verses.5:23: And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll, and shall blot them out with the most bitter waters into which he has gathered curses,
verses.5:24: and shall give them to her to drink. When she has drained them,
verses.5:25: the priest shall take from her hand the sacrifice of jealousy, and shall lift it up before the Lord, and shall place it upon the altar, provided, however, that first
verses.5:26: he take a handful of the sacrifice from what is offered and burn it upon the altar, and thus give the woman the most bitter waters to drink.
verses.5:27: When she has drunk them, if she has been defiled and, having despised her husband, is guilty of adultery, the waters of the curse will pass through her, and with her belly swollen, her thigh will rot away; and the woman will become a curse and an example to all the people.
verses.5:28: But if she has not been defiled, she will be innocent, and she will bear children.
verses.5:29: This is the law of jealousy. If a woman has turned aside from her husband, and if she has been defiled,
verses.5:30: and the husband, stirred up by a spirit of jealousy, has brought her into the sight of the Lord, and the priest has done to her according to all that is written:
verses.5:31: the husband will be without guilt, and she will receive her iniquity."
verses.6:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.6:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: A man or a woman, when they make a vow to be sanctified and wish to consecrate themselves to the Lord,
verses.6:3: they shall abstain from wine and from everything that can intoxicate. Vinegar from wine and from any other drink, and whatever is pressed from the grape, they shall not drink; fresh and dried grapes they shall not eat
verses.6:4: all the days during which they are consecrated to the Lord by a vow; whatever can come from the vine, from the raisin even to the seed, they shall not eat.
verses.6:5: Throughout the entire time of his separation, no razor shall pass over his head until the day is completed for which he is consecrated to the Lord. He shall be holy, as the locks of his head grow.
verses.6:6: Throughout the entire time of his consecration, he shall not go in to a dead person,
verses.6:7: not even over the dead body of his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister shall he be contaminated, because the consecration of his God is upon his head.
verses.6:8: All the days of his separation he shall be holy to the Lord.
verses.6:9: But if anyone dies suddenly before him, the head of his consecration will be defiled; and he shall shave it immediately on that same day of his purification, and again on the seventh.
verses.6:10: Then on the eighth day he shall offer two turtledoves or two young doves to the priest at the entrance of the covenant of the testimony.
verses.6:11: And the priest shall prepare one for sin and the other as a burnt offering, and he shall intercede for him, because he sinned on account of a dead person; and he shall sanctify his head on that day,
verses.6:12: and he shall consecrate to the Lord the days of his separation, offering a year-old lamb for sin, yet in such a way that the previous days become void, since his sanctification has been defiled.
verses.6:13: This is the law of consecration. When the days that he had determined by a vow are completed, he shall bring him to the doorway of the tabernacle of the covenant,
verses.6:14: and shall present his offerings to the Lord: an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering, and an unblemished year-old ewe for sin, and an unblemished ram as a peace offering,
verses.6:15: also a basket of unleavened loaves that are mixed with oil, and wafers without leaven anointed with oil, and the drink offerings of each one,
verses.6:16: which the priest shall offer before the Lord, and he shall prepare both the offering for sin and the burnt offering.
verses.6:17: But the ram he shall sacrifice as a peace offering to the Lord, offering at the same time the basket of unleavened loaves and the drink offerings that are due by custom.
verses.6:18: Then the Nazirite shall be shaved of the locks of his consecration before the doorway of the tabernacle of the covenant; and he shall take his hair and place it upon the fire that is set beneath the sacrifice of the peace offerings;
verses.6:19: and he shall deliver the cooked shoulder of the ram, and one cake without leaven from the basket, and one unleavened wafer into the hands of the Nazirite, after his head has been shaved.
verses.6:20: And having received them back from him, he shall lift them up in the sight of the Lord; and once sanctified, they shall belong to the priest, just like the breast that was commanded to be separated, and the thigh. After these things, the Nazirite may drink wine.
verses.6:21: This is the law of the Nazirite, when he has vowed his offering to the Lord during the time of his consecration, apart from those things that his hand has found; according to what he had vowed in his mind, so he shall do for the completion of his sanctification."
verses.6:22: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.6:23: "Speak to Aaron and his sons: In this way you shall bless the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them:
verses.6:24: 'May the Lord bless you and guard you.
verses.6:25: May the Lord show His face to you and have mercy on you.
verses.6:26: May the Lord turn His countenance toward you and give you peace.'
verses.6:27: And they shall invoke My name upon the sons of Israel, and I will bless them."
verses.7:1: Now it happened on the day when Moses completed the tabernacle, and erected it, and anointed and consecrated it along with all its vessels, similarly the altar and all its vessels,
verses.7:2: that the chiefs of Israel and the heads of the families, who were in each tribe, and the overseers of those who had been numbered, presented
verses.7:3: gifts before the Lord: six covered wagons with twelve oxen. Two leaders presented one wagon, and each of them one ox, and they presented them in the sight of the tabernacle.
verses.7:4: Then the Lord said to Moses,
verses.7:5: "Accept them from them so that they may serve in the service of the tabernacle, and you will hand them over to the Levites according to the order of their service."
verses.7:6: So when Moses had accepted the wagons and the oxen, he handed them over to the Levites.
verses.7:7: Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to what they needed.
verses.7:8: Four other wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari according to their duties and their service, under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
verses.7:9: To the sons of Kohath, however, he did not give wagons and oxen, because they serve in the sanctuary and carry the burdens on their own shoulders.
verses.7:10: Therefore, for the dedication of the altar, on the day when it was anointed, the leaders presented their offering before the altar.
verses.7:11: And the Lord said to Moses, "Let each leader on each day present gifts for the dedication of the altar."
verses.7:12: On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, presented his offering;
verses.7:13: and in it were a silver dish one hundred thirty shekels in weight, a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of fine flour moistened with oil for a sacrifice;
verses.7:14: a small mortar made of ten gold shekels, full of incense;
verses.7:15: an ox from the herd, and a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering;
verses.7:16: and a male goat for sin;
verses.7:17: and for a sacrifice of peace offerings two oxen, five rams, five male goats, five one-year-old lambs. This is the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

verses.7:89: And whenever Moses entered the tabernacle of the covenant to consult the oracle, he heard the voice of the One speaking to him from the mercy seat that was above the ark of the testimony, between the two cherubim, from where He also spoke to him.
verses.8:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.8:2: "Speak to Aaron, and you shall say to him, 'When you place the seven lamps, let the lampstand be set up on the south side.' Therefore command this, that the lamps face toward the north, directly opposite the table of the loaves of presentation; toward that side which the lampstand faces, they must shine."
verses.8:3: And Aaron did so, and placed the lamps upon the lampstand, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.8:4: Now this was the workmanship of the lampstand, of hammered gold: both the central shaft and all that sprang forth from both sides of the branches. According to the pattern that the Lord showed Moses, so he crafted the lampstand.
verses.8:5: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.8:6: "Take the Levites from the midst of the sons of Israel, and you shall purify them
verses.8:7: according to this rite: let them be sprinkled with the water of purification, and let them shave all the hair of their flesh. And when they have washed their garments and have been cleansed,
verses.8:8: they shall take an ox from the herds, and its offering, fine flour mixed with oil; but another ox from the herd you shall take for sin;
verses.8:9: and you shall bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the covenant, with the whole multitude of the sons of Israel called together.
verses.8:10: And when the Levites are before the Lord, the sons of Israel shall lay their hands upon them.
verses.8:11: And Aaron shall offer the Levites as a gift in the sight of the Lord from the sons of Israel, so that they may serve in His ministry.
verses.8:12: The Levites also shall lay their hands upon the heads of the oxen, one of which you shall offer for sin, and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord, so that you may intercede for them.
verses.8:13: And you shall station the Levites in the sight of Aaron and his sons, and you shall consecrate them, offered to the Lord,
verses.8:14: and you shall separate them from the midst of the sons of Israel, so that they may be Mine.
verses.8:15: And afterward they shall enter the tabernacle of the covenant, so that they may serve Me. And thus you shall purify and consecrate them as an offering to the Lord, for they have been given as a gift to Me by the sons of Israel.
verses.8:16: In place of the firstborn that open every womb in Israel, I have taken them.
verses.8:17: For all the firstborn of the sons of Israel are Mine, both of humans and of beasts. From the day on which I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them to Myself,
verses.8:18: and I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel,
verses.8:19: and I have given them as a gift to Aaron and his sons from the midst of the people, so that they may serve Me on behalf of Israel in the tabernacle of the covenant, and pray for them, so that there may not be a plague among the people if they should dare to approach the sanctuary."
verses.8:20: And Moses and Aaron and the whole multitude of the sons of Israel did to the Levites what the Lord had commanded Moses;
verses.8:21: and they were purified, and washed their garments. And Aaron lifted them up in the sight of the Lord, and prayed for them,
verses.8:22: so that, purified, they might enter upon their duties in the tabernacle of the covenant before Aaron and his sons. Just as the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so it was done.
verses.8:23: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.8:24: "This is the law of the Levites: from twenty-five years and upward, they shall enter to minister in the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.8:25: And when they have completed the fiftieth year of age, they shall cease to serve,
verses.8:26: and they shall be attendants of their brothers in the tabernacle of the covenant, so that they may keep watch over what was entrusted to them; but the works themselves they shall not do. Thus you shall make arrangements for the Levites in their charges."
verses.9:1: The Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying,
verses.9:2: "Let the sons of Israel keep the Passover at its time,
verses.9:3: on the fourteenth day of this month at evening, according to all its ceremonies and ordinances."
verses.9:4: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel to keep the Passover.
verses.9:5: And they kept it at its time, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, on Mount Sinai. The sons of Israel did according to all that the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.9:6: Now certain men, unclean on account of the soul of a person, who were not able to keep the Passover on that day, approaching Moses and Aaron,
verses.9:7: said to them, "We are unclean on account of the soul of a person; why are we deprived, so that we are unable to offer an offering to the Lord at its time among the sons of Israel?"
verses.9:8: Moses answered them, "Wait, so that I may inquire what the Lord commands concerning you."
verses.9:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.9:10: "Speak to the sons of Israel: 'A person who is unclean on account of a soul, or far away on a journey in your nation, shall keep the Passover to the Lord
verses.9:11: in the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening. With unleavened bread and wild lettuce they shall eat it;
verses.9:12: they shall not leave anything of it until morning, and they shall not break a bone of it; they shall observe the entire rite of the Passover.
verses.9:13: But if anyone is both clean and was not on a journey, and yet did not keep the Passover, that soul shall be cut off from his peoples, because he did not offer the sacrifice to the Lord at its time; he himself shall bear his sin.
verses.9:14: A foreigner also and a sojourner, if they are among you, shall keep the Passover to the Lord according to its ceremonies and ordinances. The same precept shall be among you both for the sojourner and for the native.'"
verses.9:15: So on the day on which the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it. And from evening over the tent there was something like the appearance of fire until morning.
verses.9:16: So it happened continually: by day the cloud covered it, and by night something like the appearance of fire.
verses.9:17: And when the cloud that sheltered the tabernacle was taken away, then the sons of Israel set out; and in the place where the cloud stopped, there they encamped.
verses.9:18: At the command of the Lord they set out, and at His command they pitched the tabernacle. All the days on which the cloud stood over the tabernacle, they remained in the same place;
verses.9:19: and if it happened that it remained over it for a long time, the sons of Israel were on watch for the Lord and did not set out
verses.9:20: for as many days as the cloud was over the tabernacle. At the command of the Lord they set up the tents, and at His command they took them down.
verses.9:21: If the cloud was there from evening until morning, and immediately at daybreak left the tabernacle, they set out; and if after a day and a night it withdrew, they dismantled the tents.
verses.9:22: But if for two days or one month or a longer time it was over the tabernacle, the sons of Israel remained in the same place and did not set out; but as soon as it withdrew, they moved camp.
verses.9:23: By the word of the Lord they pitched the tents, and by His word they set out; and they were on watch for the Lord according to His command by the hand of Moses.
verses.10:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.10:2: "Make for yourself two hammered silver trumpets, with which you may summon the multitude when the camp is to be moved.
verses.10:3: And when you sound the trumpets, the whole crowd will gather to you at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.10:4: If you blow once, the leaders and the heads of the multitude of Israel will come to you.
verses.10:5: But if a longer and broken blast sounds, those who are on the eastern side shall move camp first.
verses.10:6: And at the second sound and a similar alarm blast of the trumpet, those who dwell toward the south shall take up their tents; and the rest shall do in this manner, as the trumpets sound an alarm for departure.
verses.10:7: But when the people are to be gathered, there shall be a simple blast of the trumpets, and they shall not sound a broken alarm.
verses.10:8: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and this shall be a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations.
verses.10:9: If you go out to war from your land against adversaries who fight against you, you shall blow with trumpets sounding an alarm, and there will be a remembrance of you before the Lord your God, so that you may be rescued from the hands of your enemies.
verses.10:10: Whenever you have a banquet, and festival days, and the first days of the month, you shall sound the trumpets over the burnt offerings and the peace sacrifices, so that they may be for you a remembrance of your God. I am the Lord your God."
verses.10:11: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was lifted up from the tabernacle of the covenant,
verses.10:12: and the sons of Israel set out by their companies from the desert of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.10:13: And they moved camp first according to the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses:
verses.10:14: the sons of Judah by their companies, whose leader was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
verses.10:15: In the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the leader was Nethanel the son of Zuar.
verses.10:16: In the tribe of Zebulun, the leader was Eliab the son of Helon.
verses.10:17: And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and Merari went out carrying it.
verses.10:18: And the sons of Reuben also set out by their companies and their order, whose leader was Elizur the son of Shedeur.
verses.10:19: And in the tribe of the sons of Simeon, the leader was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
verses.10:20: Furthermore, in the tribe of Gad, the leader was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
verses.10:21: And the Kohathites also set out, carrying the sanctuary. The tabernacle was carried all the while until they came to the place of setting it up.
verses.10:22: The sons of Ephraim also moved camp by their companies, in whose army the leader was Elishama the son of Ammihud.
verses.10:23: And in the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the leader was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
verses.10:24: And in the tribe of Benjamin, the commander was Abidan the son of Gideon.
verses.10:25: Last of all the camps, the sons of Dan set out by their companies, in whose army the leader was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
verses.10:26: And in the tribe of the sons of Asher, the leader was Pagiel the son of Ochran.
verses.10:27: And in the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, the leader was Ahira the son of Enan.
verses.10:28: These are the camps and departures of the sons of Israel by their companies when they went out.
verses.10:29: And Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, his relative: "We are setting out for the place that the Lord is going to give us; come with us, so that we may do good to you, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel."
verses.10:30: He answered him, "I will not go with you, but I will return to my own land, in which I was born."
verses.10:31: And he said, "Do not leave us, for you know in which places through the desert we ought to pitch camp, and you will be our guide.
verses.10:32: And when you come with us, whatever is best from the riches that the Lord is going to deliver to us, we will give to you."
verses.10:33: Therefore they set out from the mountain of the Lord a journey of three days, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord went ahead of them, for three days providing a place for the camp.
verses.10:34: The cloud of the Lord was also over them by day when they marched.
verses.10:35: And when the ark was lifted up, Moses would say, "Rise up, Lord, and let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee from Your face."
verses.10:36: And when it was set down, he would say, "Return, Lord, to the multitude of the army of Israel."
verses.11:1: Meanwhile a murmuring of the people, as of those grieving over hardship, arose against the Lord. When the Lord heard this, He became angry. And the fire of the Lord, kindled against them, devoured the outermost part of the camp.
verses.11:2: And when the people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire was swallowed up.
verses.11:3: And he called the name of that place Burning, because the fire of the Lord had been kindled against them.
verses.11:4: For the mixed rabble that had gone up with them burned with craving, sitting and weeping, with the sons of Israel likewise joined to them, and said, "Who will give us meat to eat?
verses.11:5: We remember the fish that we used to eat in Egypt at no cost; into our mind come the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic.
verses.11:6: Our soul is dried up; our eyes look upon nothing else except manna."
verses.11:7: Now the manna was like coriander seed, of the color of bdellium.
verses.11:8: And the people went around, and gathering it, ground it with a millstone or pounded it in a mortar, cooking it in a pot and making from it small cakes with a taste like oiled bread.
verses.11:9: And when the dew descended upon the camp at night, the manna also descended along with it.
verses.11:10: Therefore Moses heard the people weeping by families, each one at the entrance of his tent. And the wrath of the Lord was greatly angered, and to Moses also the matter seemed unbearable,
verses.11:11: and he said to the Lord, "Why have You afflicted Your servant? Why do I not find favor before You? And why have You laid the weight of this entire people upon me?
verses.11:12: Did I conceive all this multitude, or give birth to it, that You should say to me, 'Carry them in your bosom as a nurse is accustomed to carry a little infant, and bring them to the land concerning which You swore to their fathers'?
verses.11:13: Where can I get meat to give to so great a multitude? They weep against me, saying, 'Give us meat so that we may eat.'
verses.11:14: I cannot bear all this people alone, because it is heavy for me.
verses.11:15: But if it seems otherwise to You, I beg that You kill me, and that I may find favor in Your eyes, so that I may not be afflicted with such great evils."
verses.11:16: And the Lord said to Moses, "Gather to Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and overseers; and you shall lead them to the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant, and make them stand there with you,
verses.11:17: so that I may come down and speak to you; and I will take from your spirit and impart it to them, so that they may bear with you the burden of the people, and you alone may not be burdened.
verses.11:18: And to the people also you shall say, 'Sanctify yourselves (tomorrow you will eat meat, for I have heard you say, "Who will give us meat for food? It was well with us in Egypt"), so that the Lord may give you meat, and you may eat,
verses.11:19: not for one day, nor two, or five, or ten, nor even twenty,
verses.11:20: but up to a month of days, until it comes out through your nostrils and turns into nausea, because you have rejected the Lord, who is in the middle of you, and have wept before Him, saying, "Why did we come out of Egypt?"'"
verses.11:21: And Moses said, "There are six hundred thousand men on foot in this people, and You say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month'?
verses.11:22: Will a multitude of sheep and oxen be slaughtered, so that it can suffice for food? Or will all the fish of the sea be gathered together, so that they may satisfy them?"
verses.11:23: The Lord answered him, "Is the hand of the Lord powerless? Right now you will see whether My word is fulfilled in deed."
verses.11:24: Moses therefore came and told the people the words of the Lord, gathering seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom he made to stand around the tabernacle.
verses.11:25: And the Lord descended through the cloud and spoke to him, taking from the spirit that was in Moses and giving it to the seventy men. And when the spirit had rested in them, they prophesied, and did not cease anymore.
verses.11:26: Now two men had remained in the camp, one of whom was called Eldad, and the other Medad, upon whom the spirit rested. For they too had been enrolled, and had not gone out to the tabernacle.
verses.11:27: And while they were prophesying in the camp, a boy ran and reported to Moses, saying, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."
verses.11:28: Immediately Joshua the son of Nun, the attendant of Moses and chosen from among many, said, "My lord Moses, forbid them."
verses.11:29: But he said, "Why are you jealous for my sake? Who would grant that all the people might prophesy, and that the Lord would give them His Spirit?"
verses.11:30: And Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.
verses.11:31: Now a wind going out from the Lord, sweeping up quail from across the sea, brought them and dropped them into the camp, as far as a journey that can be completed in one day on every side of the camp all around, and they were flying in the air at a height of two cubits above the ground.
verses.11:32: Therefore the people, rising up all that day, and the night, and the next day, gathered quail; the one who gathered little gathered ten kors; and they dried them all around the camp.
verses.11:33: The meat was still in their teeth, and food of this kind had not failed, and look, the wrath of the Lord, aroused against the people, struck them with an exceedingly great plague.
verses.11:34: And that place was called Graves of Craving, for there they buried the people who had craved. And having gone out from Graves of Craving, they came to Hazeroth and remained there.
verses.12:1: And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses on account of his Ethiopian wife,
verses.12:2: and they said, "Has the Lord spoken through Moses alone? Has He not also spoken to us in the same way?" When the Lord had heard this
verses.12:3: (for Moses was a most gentle man, above all people who lived on the earth),
verses.12:4: He spoke at once to him, and to Aaron and Miriam, "Go out, the three of you alone, to the tabernacle of the covenant." And when they had gone out,
verses.12:5: the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tabernacle, calling Aaron and Miriam. When they had come,
verses.12:6: He said to them, "Hear My words: if anyone among you is a prophet of the Lord, I will appear to him in a vision, or I will speak to him through a dream.
verses.12:7: But My servant Moses, who is most faithful in all My house, is not like that:
verses.12:8: for I speak to him mouth to mouth; and openly, and not through riddles and figures, he sees the Lord. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak ill of My servant Moses?"
verses.12:9: And angry against them, He departed.
verses.12:10: The cloud that was over the tabernacle also withdrew, and look, Miriam appeared bright white with leprosy, like snow. And when Aaron had turned to look at her and seen her covered all over with leprosy,
verses.12:11: he said to Moses, "I implore you, my lord, do not lay upon us this sin that we have foolishly committed;
verses.12:12: do not let her become like one who is dead, and like a stillborn child that is cast out from its mother's womb; look, already half of her flesh has been devoured by leprosy."
verses.12:13: And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, "God, I implore You, heal her."
verses.12:14: The Lord answered him, "If her father had spit in her face, should she not have been flushed with shame for at least seven days? Let her be separated outside the camp for seven days, and afterward she will be called back."
verses.12:15: Therefore Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move from that place until Miriam was called back.
verses.13:1: And the people set out from Hazeroth, pitching their tents in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.13:2: And there the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.13:3: "Send men to examine the land of Canaan, which I am about to give to the sons of Israel, one from each tribe, from among the leaders."
verses.13:4: Moses did what the Lord had commanded, sending leading men from the wilderness of Paran, whose names are these:
verses.13:5: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur.
verses.13:6: From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
verses.13:7: From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
verses.13:8: From the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph.
verses.13:9: From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun.
verses.13:10: From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu.
verses.13:11: From the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi.
verses.13:12: From the tribe of Joseph, of the scepter of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi.
verses.13:13: From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.
verses.13:14: From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.
verses.13:15: From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi.
verses.13:16: From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
verses.13:17: These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to examine the land; and he called Hoshea, son of Nun, Joshua.
verses.13:18: So Moses sent them to examine the land of Canaan, and said to them, "Go up through the southern region. And when you come to the mountains,
verses.13:19: examine the land, what kind it is, and the people who are its inhabitants, whether they are strong or weak, whether few in number or many;
verses.13:20: the land itself, good or bad; what the cities are like, walled or without walls;
verses.13:21: the soil, rich or barren, wooded or without trees. Take courage, and bring us some of the fruits of the land." Now it was the season when the early grapes can already be eaten.
verses.13:22: And when they had gone up, they scouted the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, as one enters Hamath.
verses.13:23: And they went up to the south and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the sons of Anak, were; for Hebron was founded seven years before Tanis, a city of Egypt.
verses.13:24: And going on as far as the Stream of the Cluster, they cut off a vine branch with its bunch of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took some of the pomegranates and the figs of that place,
verses.13:25: which was called Nehelescol, that is, the Stream of the Cluster, because the sons of Israel had carried a cluster from there.
verses.13:26: And the scouts of the land, returning after forty days, having traveled around the entire region,
verses.13:27: came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Paran, which is in Kadesh. And speaking to them and to the whole multitude, they showed the fruits of the land,
verses.13:28: and they reported, saying, "We came into the land to which you sent us, which truly flows with milk and honey, as can be known from these fruits;
verses.13:29: but it has very strong inhabitants, and large and walled cities. We saw the offspring of Anak there.
verses.13:30: Amalek lives in the south; the Hittites, the Jebusites, and the Amorites in the hill country; while the Canaanites dwell beside the sea and along the streams of the Jordan."
verses.13:31: Meanwhile, Caleb, quieting the murmuring of the people, who were rising up against Moses, said, "Let us go up and possess the land, for we will be able to obtain it."
verses.13:32: But the others, who had been with him, were saying, "By no means are we able to go up against this people, because they are stronger than we are."
verses.13:33: And before the sons of Israel they spoke ill of the land that they had inspected, saying, "The land that we traversed devours its inhabitants; the people whom we looked upon are of tall stature.
verses.13:34: There we saw certain monsters of the sons of Anak, of the giant race, compared to whom we seemed like locusts."
verses.14:1: Therefore, crying out loudly, the whole crowd wept that night,
verses.14:2: and all the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.14:3: "If only we had died in Egypt! And in this vast wilderness, if only we might perish, and may the Lord not lead us into this land, so that we do not fall by the sword and our wives and children are not led away captive. Is it not better to return to Egypt?"
verses.14:4: And they said to one another, "Let us appoint a leader for ourselves, and let us return to Egypt."
verses.14:5: Upon hearing this, Moses and Aaron fell face down to the ground before the whole multitude of the sons of Israel.
verses.14:6: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who had themselves also surveyed the land, tore their garments,
verses.14:7: and spoke to the whole multitude of the sons of Israel: "The land that we traversed is exceedingly good.
verses.14:8: If the Lord is gracious, He will lead us into it, and He will hand over ground flowing with milk and honey.
verses.14:9: Do not be rebellious against the Lord, and do not fear the people of this land, for just like bread, we can devour them. All protection has departed from them. The Lord is with us; do not be afraid."
verses.14:10: And while the whole multitude was shouting and wanting to crush them with stones, the glory of the Lord appeared above the roof of the covenant to all the sons of Israel.
verses.14:11: And the Lord said to Moses, "How long will this people disparage Me? How long will they not believe Me, amid all the signs that I have done before them?
verses.14:12: Therefore I will strike them with pestilence and consume them; but I will make you a ruler over a nation great and stronger than this one is."
verses.14:13: And Moses said to the Lord, "So that the Egyptians, from whose midst You brought out this people,
verses.14:14: and the inhabitants of this land, who have heard that You, Lord, are among this people, and are seen face to face, and Your cloud protects them, and in a pillar of cloud You go before them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night,
verses.14:15: may hear that You have killed so great a multitude like one man, and may say,
verses.14:16: 'He was not able to bring the people into the land concerning which He had sworn; therefore He killed them in the wilderness'?
verses.14:17: Therefore let the strength of the Lord be magnified, just as You swore, saying,
verses.14:18: 'The Lord, patient and of great mercy, taking away iniquity and wicked deeds, and leaving no one guiltless, You who visit the sins of the fathers upon the sons to the third and fourth generation.'
verses.14:19: Forgive, I implore You, the sin of this people according to the greatness of Your mercy, just as You have been gracious to those coming out of Egypt up to this place."
verses.14:20: And the Lord said, "I have forgiven according to your word.
verses.14:21: As I live, the whole earth will be filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.14:22: Yet all the men who have seen My majesty and the signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have now tested Me ten times and have not obeyed My voice,
verses.14:23: will not see the land concerning which I swore to their fathers, nor will anyone among those who disparaged Me look upon it.
verses.14:24: My servant Caleb, who is full of another spirit and has followed Me, I will lead into this land that he traversed; and his seed will possess it.
verses.14:25: Since the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valleys, tomorrow move camp and return into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea."
verses.14:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.14:27: "How long does this most wicked multitude grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints of the sons of Israel.
verses.14:28: Therefore say to them, 'As I live, says the Lord, just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you.
verses.14:29: In this wilderness your corpses will lie. All of you who were numbered from twenty years old and upward, and grumbled against Me,
verses.14:30: will not enter the land over which I raised My hand to make you dwell in it, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.14:31: But your little ones, of whom you said that they would be prey for enemies, I will bring in, so that they may see the land that displeased you.
verses.14:32: Your corpses will lie in the wilderness.
verses.14:33: Your sons will be wanderers in the desert for forty years, and they will bear your fornication, until the corpses of the fathers are consumed in the desert,
verses.14:34: according to the number of the forty days in which you examined the land: a year will be reckoned for a day. And for forty years you will receive your iniquities, and you will know My vengeance:
verses.14:35: for just as I have spoken, so I will do to all this most wicked multitude that has risen up against Me: in this wilderness it will come to an end and die.'"
verses.14:36: Therefore all the men whom Moses had sent to observe the land, and who, having returned, had made the whole multitude grumble against him, disparaging the land as being bad,
verses.14:37: died and were struck down in the sight of the Lord.
verses.14:38: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh lived, out of all those who had gone to examine the land.
verses.14:39: And Moses spoke all these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
verses.14:40: And look, rising very early in the morning, they went up to the summit of the mountain and said, "We are ready to go up to the place of which the Lord has spoken, for we have sinned."
verses.14:41: To them Moses said, "Why do you transgress the word of the Lord, which will not turn out favorably for you?
verses.14:42: Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, so that you do not fall before your enemies.
verses.14:43: The Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, by whose sword you will fall, because you were unwilling to submit to the Lord; nor will the Lord be with you."
verses.14:44: But they, darkened, went up to the summit of the mountain. Yet the ark of the covenant of the Lord and Moses did not depart from the camp.
verses.14:45: And the Amalekite and the Canaanite, who dwelt on the mountain, came down, and striking them and cutting them down, pursued them as far as Hormah.
verses.15:1: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.15:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'When you have entered the land of your dwelling, which I will give to you,
verses.15:3: and have made an offering to the Lord as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, paying vows, or willingly offering gifts, or in your solemn feasts burning a fragrance of sweetness to the Lord, from the oxen or from the sheep,
verses.15:4: whoever slaughters a sacrificial victim shall offer a sacrifice of fine flour, a tenth part of an ephah, mixed with oil that shall have the measure of a fourth part of a hin;
verses.15:5: and he shall give wine for pouring drink offerings of the same measure for a burnt offering or for a sacrifice. For individual lambs
verses.15:6: and rams there shall be a sacrifice of two tenths of fine flour, which shall be mixed with oil of a third part of a hin;
verses.15:7: and he shall offer wine for a drink offering of a third part of the same measure for a fragrance of sweetness to the Lord.
verses.15:8: But when you make a burnt offering or a sacrifice from the oxen, to fulfill a vow or peace offerings,
verses.15:9: you shall give for each ox three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil that shall have half the measure of a hin,
verses.15:10: and wine for pouring drink offerings of the same measure, for an offering of the sweetest fragrance to the Lord.
verses.15:12: for each ox and ram and lamb and young goat.
verses.15:14: shall offer sacrifices by the same rite.
verses.15:15: There shall be one precept and judgment both for you and for the strangers of the land.'"
verses.15:16: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.15:17: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them,
verses.15:18: 'When you come into the land that I will give to you,
verses.15:19: and eat from the breads of that region, you shall set apart firstfruits to the Lord
verses.15:20: from your foods. Just as you set apart firstfruits from the threshing floors,
verses.15:21: so also from the cooked dishes you shall give firstfruits to the Lord.
verses.15:22: But if through ignorance you omit any of these things that the Lord has spoken to Moses,
verses.15:23: and has commanded to you through him, from the day on which He began to command and onward,
verses.15:24: and the multitude has forgotten to do so, it shall offer a calf from the herd as a burnt offering for a most sweet fragrance to the Lord, and its sacrifice and drink offerings, as the ceremonies require, and a male goat for sin;
verses.15:25: and the priest shall pray for the whole multitude of the sons of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them, because they did not sin willingly, nevertheless offering incense to the Lord for themselves and for their sin and error;
verses.15:26: and it shall be forgiven to the entire populace of the sons of Israel and to the strangers who sojourn among them, because it is a fault of all the people through ignorance.
verses.15:27: But if one soul sins unknowingly, he shall offer a year-old female goat for his sin;
verses.15:28: and the priest shall intercede for him, because he sinned unknowingly before the Lord; and he shall obtain pardon for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
verses.15:29: Both for the native-born and for the strangers, there shall be one law for all who sin in ignorance.
verses.15:30: But the soul who commits anything through pride, whether he is a citizen or a foreigner, because he has been rebellious against the Lord, shall perish from his people;
verses.15:31: for he has despised the word of the Lord and has made His precept void; therefore he shall be wiped out, and he shall bear his iniquity.'"
verses.15:32: Now it happened that when the sons of Israel were in the wilderness and had found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day,
verses.15:33: they brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the entire multitude.
verses.15:34: And they confined him in prison, not knowing what they ought to do concerning him.
verses.15:35: And the Lord said to Moses, "Let this man surely die; let the whole crowd overwhelm him with stones outside the camp."
verses.15:36: And when they had led him outside, they overwhelmed him with stones, and he died, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.15:37: The Lord also said to Moses,
verses.15:38: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them to make for themselves fringes along the corners of their cloaks, placing blue-violet ribbons in them,
verses.15:39: so that when they see them, they may remember all the commandments of the Lord, and may not follow their own thoughts and eyes, prostituting themselves among various things,
verses.15:40: but rather, mindful of the precepts of the Lord, may do them, and may be holy to their God.
verses.15:41: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I might be your God."
verses.16:1: Now look, Korah the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and also On the son of Peleth, of the sons of Reuben,
verses.16:2: rose up against Moses, together with two hundred fifty other men of the sons of Israel, leaders of the assembly, and those who were called by name at the time of council.
verses.16:3: And when they had stood against Moses and Aaron, they said, "Let it be enough for you, since the whole multitude consists of holy ones, and the Lord is among them; why do you exalt yourselves above the people of the Lord?"
verses.16:4: When Moses heard this, he fell prostrate on his face;
verses.16:5: and speaking to Korah and to the whole multitude, "In the morning," he said, "the Lord will make known who belong to Him, and He will draw the holy ones to Himself; and those whom He chooses will draw near to Him.
verses.16:6: Therefore do this: let everyone take their censers, you, Korah, and all your council;
verses.16:7: and tomorrow, having drawn fire, put incense on top before the Lord; and whomever He chooses, he shall be holy. You raise yourselves up too much, sons of Levi."
verses.16:8: And he said again to Korah, "Listen, sons of Levi:
verses.16:9: is it too little for you that the God of Israel has separated you from all the people and joined you to Himself, so that you might serve Him in the worship of the tabernacle, and stand before the throng of the people, and minister to Him?
verses.16:10: Did He therefore cause you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, to draw near to Himself, so that you might also claim the priesthood for yourselves,
verses.16:11: and that your entire band might stand against the Lord? For what is Aaron, that you murmur against him?"
verses.16:12: Therefore Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. And they answered, "We are not coming.
verses.16:13: Is it too little for you that you brought us out of a land that flowed with milk and honey, to kill us in the desert, unless you also rule over us?
verses.16:14: Indeed, you have brought us into a land that flows with streams of milk and honey, and have given us possessions of fields and vineyards; or do you also want to gouge out our eyes? We are not coming."
verses.16:15: And Moses, becoming very angry, said to the Lord, "Do not regard their sacrifices; You know that I have never taken even a little donkey from them, nor have I afflicted any one of them."
verses.16:16: And he said to Korah, "You and all your congregation, stand apart before the Lord, and Aaron separately tomorrow.
verses.16:17: Take each of you your censers, and put incense upon them, offering to the Lord two hundred fifty censers; let Aaron also hold his censer."
verses.16:18: When they had done this, while Moses and Aaron were standing,
verses.16:19: and had amassed the whole multitude against them at the entrance of the tabernacle, the glory of the Lord appeared to all.
verses.16:20: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.16:21: "Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, so that I may suddenly destroy them."
verses.16:22: And they fell prostrate on their faces and said, "Most mighty God of the spirits of all flesh, when one sins, will Your wrath rage against all?"
verses.16:23: And the Lord said to Moses,
verses.16:24: "Command the entire people to separate themselves from the tents of Korah and Dathan and Abiram."
verses.16:25: And Moses rose up and went to Dathan and Abiram; and with the elders of Israel following him,
verses.16:26: he said to the crowd, "Depart from the tents of the wicked men, and do not touch what belongs to them, so that you may not be entangled in their sins."
verses.16:27: And when they had departed from their tents all around, Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their pavilions with their wives and children and all the throng.
verses.16:28: And Moses said, "By this you will know that the Lord has sent me to do all the things that you see, and that I have not brought them forth from my own heart:
verses.16:29: if they perish by the ordinary death of men, and a stroke visits them with which the rest also are accustomed to be visited, the Lord has not sent me;
verses.16:30: but if the Lord does a new thing, so that the earth, opening its mouth, swallows them up and all things that belong to them, and they go down alive into the underworld, you will know that they have blasphemed the Lord."
verses.16:31: Immediately, therefore, as he ceased speaking, the earth split apart beneath their feet,
verses.16:32: and opening its mouth, it devoured them with their tents and all their possessions;
verses.16:33: and they went down alive into the underworld, covered with earth, and perished from the midst of the multitude.
verses.16:34: But all Israel, who was standing all around, fled at the cry of those who were perishing, saying, "The earth might swallow us up too!"
verses.16:35: Moreover, fire coming out from the Lord killed the two hundred fifty men who were offering incense.
verses.16:36: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.16:37: "Command Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron, to take up the censers that lie in the blaze and scatter the fire here and there, since they have been sanctified
verses.16:38: in the deaths of the sinners; and let him beat them out into plates and fasten them to the altar, because incense was offered in them to the Lord and they have been sanctified, so that the sons of Israel may see them as a sign and a reminder."
verses.16:39: Therefore Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers in which those whom the blaze devoured had offered, and beat them out into plates, fastening them to the altar,
verses.16:40: so that afterward the sons of Israel might have things by which to be reminded that no outsider, and no one who is not of the seed of Aaron, may approach to offer incense to the Lord, so that he may not suffer as Korah and all his congregation suffered, as the Lord spoke to Moses.
verses.16:41: Now the whole multitude of the sons of Israel grumbled on the following day against Moses and Aaron, saying, "You have killed the people of the Lord."
verses.16:42: And when a rebellion arose and the uproar grew,
verses.16:43: Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. After they entered it, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
verses.16:44: Then the Lord said to Moses:
verses.16:45: "Withdraw from the midst of this multitude; even now I will destroy them." And while they were lying on the ground,
verses.16:46: Moses said to Aaron, "Take the censer, and having drawn fire from the altar, put incense on top, going quickly to the people so that you may pray for them; for wrath has already gone out from the Lord, and the plague is raging."
verses.16:47: When Aaron had done this and had run into the midst of the multitude, which the blaze was already devastating, he offered the incense,
verses.16:48: and standing between the dead and the living, he pleaded for the people, and the plague ceased.
verses.16:49: Now those who were struck down were fourteen thousand seven hundred people, apart from those who had perished in the rebellion of Korah.
verses.16:50: And Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant after the destruction had subsided.
verses.17:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.17:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel and receive from them one rod each according to their clans, from all the leaders of the tribes, twelve rods; and you shall inscribe the name of each one upon his rod.
verses.17:3: Now the name of Aaron shall be in the tribe of Levi, and one rod shall include all the families separately;
verses.17:4: and you shall place them in the tabernacle of the covenant before the testimony, where I will speak to you.
verses.17:5: He whom I choose from among these, his rod will sprout; and I will restrain from Me the complaints of the sons of Israel, with which they grumble against you."
verses.17:6: And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all the leaders gave him rods, one for each tribe; and there were twelve rods, apart from the rod of Aaron.
verses.17:7: When Moses had placed them before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony,
verses.17:8: returning on the following day, he found that the rod of Aaron in the house of Levi had sprouted; and with the buds swelling, blossoms had burst forth, which, as the leaves spread open, were formed into almonds.
verses.17:9: Therefore Moses brought out all the rods from the presence of the Lord to all the sons of Israel; and they looked, and each one received back his own rod.
verses.17:10: And the Lord said to Moses, "Bring back the rod of Aaron into the tabernacle of the testimony, so that it may be kept there as a sign for the rebellious sons of Israel, and that their complaints may subside from Me, so that they may not die."
verses.17:11: And Moses did just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.17:12: Then the sons of Israel said to Moses, "Look, we are consumed! We have all perished!
verses.17:13: Whoever approaches the tabernacle of the Lord dies. Are we all to be destroyed to utter annihilation?"
verses.18:1: And the Lord said to Aaron, "You and your sons and the house of your father with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, and you and your sons together shall bear the sins of your priesthood.
verses.18:2: Also take with you your brothers from the tribe of Levi and the scepter of your father, and let them be on hand and minister to you; but you and your sons shall minister in the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.18:3: And the Levites shall keep watch at your commands and over all the works of the tabernacle, provided only that they do not approach the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, so that neither they die nor you perish together.
