verses.18:4: Let them be with you and keep watch in the guard duties of the tabernacle and in all its ceremonies. No outsider shall mingle with you.
verses.18:5: Keep watch in the custody of the sanctuary and in the ministry of the altar, so that indignation may not arise upon the sons of Israel.
verses.18:6: I Myself have given you your brothers the Levites from the midst of the sons of Israel, and have handed them over as a gift to the Lord, so that they may serve in the ministries of His tabernacle.
verses.18:7: But you and your sons, guard your priesthood; and all things that pertain to the service of the altar and are within the veil shall be administered by the priests. If any outsider approaches, he shall be put to death."
verses.18:8: And the Lord spoke to Aaron, "Look, I have given you the custody of My firstfruits. All the things that are sanctified by the sons of Israel I have handed over to you and to your sons for the priestly office as everlasting ordinances.
verses.18:9: These things, therefore, you shall receive from those that are sanctified and have been offered to the Lord. Every offering, and sacrifice, and whatever is rendered to Me for sin and for guilt, and passes into the most holy things, shall be yours and your sons'.
verses.18:10: You shall eat it in the sanctuary; only males shall eat of it, because it has been consecrated to you.
verses.18:11: And the firstfruits that the sons of Israel vow and offer, I have given to you, and to your sons, and to your daughters, by a perpetual right; whoever is clean in your house shall eat them.
verses.18:12: All the marrow of the oil, and of the wine, and of the grain, whatever firstfruits they offer to the Lord, I have given to you.
verses.18:13: All the first produce of the crops that the ground yields and that are brought to the Lord shall go to your use; whoever is clean in your house shall eat them.
verses.18:14: Everything that the sons of Israel render by a vow shall be yours.
verses.18:15: Whatever first breaks forth from the womb of all flesh that they offer to the Lord, whether it is of human beings or of livestock, shall be yours by right, provided only that you accept a price for the firstborn of a human being and have every animal that is unclean redeemed,
verses.18:16: whose redemption shall be after one month, for five shekels of silver, by the weight of the sanctuary. A shekel has twenty obols.
verses.18:17: However, the firstborn of an ox, and of a sheep, and of a goat, you shall not have redeemed, because they have been sanctified to the Lord. Their blood alone you shall pour out upon the altar, and their fat you shall burn as a most sweet fragrance to the Lord.
verses.18:18: But the flesh shall go to your use, just like the consecrated breast and the right shoulder; they shall be yours.
verses.18:19: All the firstfruits of the sanctuary that the sons of Israel offer to the Lord I have given to you, and to your sons, and to your daughters, by a perpetual right. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the Lord for you and for your sons."
verses.18:20: And the Lord said to Aaron, "In their land you shall possess nothing, nor shall you have a portion among them; I am your portion and your inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel.
verses.18:21: And to the sons of Levi I have given all the tithes of Israel as a possession, in return for the ministry by which they serve Me in the tabernacle of the covenant,
verses.18:22: so that the sons of Israel may no longer approach the tabernacle, nor commit a deadly sin,
verses.18:23: with only the sons of Levi serving Me in the tabernacle and bearing the sins of the people. It shall be an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations. They shall possess nothing else,
verses.18:24: being content with the offering of the tithes, which I have set apart for their uses and necessities."
verses.18:25: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.18:26: "Command the Levites and declare to them, 'When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithes that I have given to you, offer the firstfruits of them to the Lord, that is, a tenth part of the tithe,
verses.18:27: so that it may be counted to you as an offering of firstfruits, both from the threshing floors and from the winepresses;
verses.18:28: and from all things whose firstfruits you receive, offer them to the Lord and give them to Aaron the priest.
verses.18:29: All the things that you offer from the tithes and set apart for the gifts of the Lord shall be the best and choicest.'
verses.18:30: And you shall say to them, 'If you offer all the finest and superior portions from the tithes, it shall be counted to you as though you had given firstfruits from the threshing floor and the winepress;
verses.18:31: and you shall eat them in all your places, both you and your families, because it is payment for the ministry by which you serve in the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.18:32: And you shall not sin in this matter by reserving the choice and fat things for yourselves, so that you may not defile the offerings of the sons of Israel and die.'"
verses.19:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.19:2: "This is the rite of the sacrifice that the Lord has established. Command the sons of Israel to bring to you a red cow of full age, in which there is no blemish and that has not borne a yoke;
verses.19:3: and you shall hand her over to Eleazar the priest, who, after she has been led outside the camp, shall sacrifice her in the sight of all;
verses.19:4: and dipping his finger in her blood, he shall sprinkle toward the doors of the tabernacle seven times,
verses.19:5: and he shall burn her while all look on, with both her hide and her flesh as well as her blood and dung committed to the flame.
verses.19:6: The priest shall also cast cedar wood, and hyssop, and twice-dyed scarlet into the flame that devours the cow.
verses.19:7: And only then, having washed his clothes and his body, shall he enter the camp, and he will be tainted until evening.
verses.19:8: Moreover, the one who has burned her shall wash his clothes and body, and he will be unclean until evening.
verses.19:9: Now a clean man shall gather the ashes of the cow and pour them out outside the camp in a most pure place, so that they may be for safekeeping and for water of sprinkling for the multitude of the sons of Israel, because the cow was burned for sin.
verses.19:10: And when the one who had carried the ashes of the cow has washed his clothes, he will be unclean until evening. The sons of Israel, and the foreigners who dwell among them, shall hold this sacred by a perpetual law.
verses.19:11: Whoever touches the corpse of a human being, and because of this is unclean for seven days,
verses.19:12: shall be sprinkled with this water on the third and the seventh day, and so will be made clean. If he has not been sprinkled on the third day, on the seventh he will not be able to be made clean.
verses.19:13: Everyone who touches the dead body of a human soul and has not been sprinkled with this mixture will defile the tabernacle of the Lord and will perish from Israel; because he has not been sprinkled with the water of expiation, he will be unclean, and his filth will remain upon him.
verses.19:14: This is the law of a man who dies in a tent: all who enter his tent, and all the vessels that are there, will be defiled for seven days.
verses.19:15: A vessel that has neither a cover nor a fastening over it will be unclean.
verses.19:16: If anyone in the field touches the corpse of a man who was killed or who died naturally, or a bone of his, or a grave, he will be unclean for seven days.
verses.19:17: And they shall take some of the ashes of the burning and of sin, and pour living waters over them into a vessel;
verses.19:18: and when a clean man has dipped hyssop into them, he shall sprinkle the entire tent with it, and all the furnishings, and the people defiled by a contagion of this kind;
verses.19:19: and in this way the clean man shall purify the unclean man on the third and the seventh day; and once cleansed on the seventh day, he shall wash both himself and his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
verses.19:20: If anyone has not been cleansed by this rite, his soul will perish from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord and has not been sprinkled with the water of purification.
verses.19:21: This shall be an everlasting lawful ordinance. He also who sprinkles the waters shall wash his clothes. Everyone who touches the waters of expiation will be unclean until evening.
verses.19:22: Whatever an unclean person touches, he will make unclean; and the soul that touches any of these things will be unclean until evening."
verses.20:1: And the sons of Israel and the whole multitude came into the desert of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Kadesh. And Miriam died there and was buried in the same place.
verses.20:2: And when the people lacked water, they assembled against Moses and Aaron,
verses.20:3: and turning to sedition, they said, "If only we had perished among our brothers before the Lord!
verses.20:4: Why have you brought the assembly of the Lord out into the wilderness, so that both we and our livestock should die?
verses.20:5: Why have you made us come up out of Egypt and brought us into this worst of places, which cannot be sown, which produces neither fig nor vines nor pomegranates, and moreover has no water to drink?"
verses.20:6: And Moses and Aaron, having left the multitude, entered the tabernacle of the covenant, fell face down to the ground, and cried out to the Lord and said, "Lord God, hear the cry of this people, and open to them Your treasure, a spring of living water, so that, once they are satisfied, their murmuring may cease." And the glory of the Lord appeared over them.
verses.20:7: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.20:8: "Take the staff, and assemble the people, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before them, and it will give waters. And when you have brought water out of the rock, the whole multitude and its livestock will drink."
verses.20:9: So Moses took the staff that was in the sight of the Lord, just as He had commanded him;
verses.20:10: and when the multitude had been assembled before the rock, he said to them, "Listen, rebels and unbelievers: can we really bring water out of this rock for you?"
verses.20:11: And when Moses had raised his hand, striking the flint twice with the staff, most abundant waters came forth, so that the people and the livestock drank.
verses.20:12: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not believe Me, so as to sanctify Me before the sons of Israel, you will not bring these peoples into the land that I will give them."
verses.20:13: This is the water of contradiction, where the sons of Israel contended against the Lord, and He was sanctified among them.
verses.20:14: Meanwhile Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom to say, "Your brother Israel sends this message: 'You know all the hardship that has overtaken us,
verses.20:15: how our fathers went down into Egypt, and we dwelt there for a long time, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers;
verses.20:16: and how we cried out to the Lord, and He heard us and sent an angel who brought us out of Egypt. Look, situated in the city of Kadesh, which is at the outermost edge of your borders,
verses.20:17: we implore that we be permitted to pass through your land. We will not go through fields or through vineyards; we will not drink waters from your wells; but we will walk along the public road, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left, until we cross your boundaries.'"
verses.20:18: Edom answered him, "You will not pass through me; otherwise I will come out armed to meet you."
verses.20:19: And the sons of Israel said, "We will walk along the beaten road; and if we drink your waters, we and our herds, we will give what is fair; there will be no difficulty over the price; only let us pass through quickly."
verses.20:20: But he answered, "You will not pass through." And immediately he went out to meet them with a countless multitude and a strong hand,
verses.20:21: and he was unwilling to yield to the one pleading with him, so as to grant passage through his borders. For this reason Israel turned away from him.
verses.20:22: And when they had moved camp from Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, which is at the borders of the land of Edom,
verses.20:23: where the Lord spoke to Moses.
verses.20:24: "Let Aaron go," He said, "to his peoples; for he will not enter the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, because he was unbelieving toward My mouth at the waters of contradiction.
verses.20:25: Take Aaron and his son with him, and you shall lead them onto Mount Hor.
verses.20:26: And when you have stripped the father of his garment, you shall clothe Eleazar his son with it; Aaron will be gathered, and he will die there."
verses.20:27: Moses did as the Lord had commanded, and they went up onto Mount Hor before the whole multitude.
verses.20:28: And when he had stripped Aaron of his garments, he clothed Eleazar his son with them.
verses.20:29: When Aaron died on the brow of the mountain, Moses came down with Eleazar.
verses.20:30: Now the whole multitude, seeing that Aaron had died, wept over him for thirty days throughout all its families.
verses.21:1: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived toward the south, heard this—namely, that Israel had come by the way of the scouts—he fought against him, and being victorious, led away plunder from him.
verses.21:2: But Israel, binding himself to the Lord by a vow, said, "If You deliver this people into my hand, I will wipe out its cities."
verses.21:3: And the Lord heard the prayers of Israel and delivered the Canaanite, whom he killed, having overthrown his cities; and he called the name of that place Hormah, that is, anathema.
verses.21:4: Now they also set out from Mount Hor by the way that leads to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. And the people began to grow weary of the journey and the hardship,
verses.21:5: and speaking against God and Moses, they said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt so that we might die in the wilderness? Bread is lacking; there is no water; our soul is now nauseated at this utterly light food."
verses.21:6: For this reason the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people; and at their strikes and the deaths of very many,
verses.21:7: they came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, because we spoke against the Lord and you; pray that He may take the serpents away from us." And Moses prayed for the people,
verses.21:8: and the Lord spoke to him, "Make a bronze serpent and set it as a sign; whoever is struck and looks at it will live."
verses.21:9: Therefore Moses made a bronze serpent and set it as a sign; and when those who were struck looked at it, they were healed.
verses.21:10: And setting out, the sons of Israel encamped at Oboth.
verses.21:11: Departing from there, they pitched tents at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab toward the eastern side.
verses.21:12: And moving from there, they came to the torrent Zered.
verses.21:13: Leaving it, they encamped opposite Arnon, which is in the desert and juts out into the borders of the Amorite. For indeed Arnon is the boundary of Moab, dividing the Moabites and the Amorites.
verses.21:14: Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord, "Just as He did in the Red Sea, so He will do in the torrents of Arnon.
verses.21:15: The cliffs of the torrents sloped down so that they might rest in Ar and recline on the borders of the Moabites."
verses.21:16: From that place a well appeared, concerning which the Lord spoke to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
verses.21:17: Then Israel sang this song: "Let the well rise up." They sang together:
verses.21:18: "The well, which the princes dug and the leaders of the multitude prepared, with the giver of the law and with their staffs." From the wilderness, Mattanah.
verses.21:19: From Mattanah to Nahaliel; from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
verses.21:20: From Bamoth there is a valley in the region of Moab, at the summit of Pisgah, which faces toward the desert.
verses.21:21: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, saying,
verses.21:22: "I beg that I may be permitted to pass through your land; we will not turn aside into fields and vineyards; we will not drink water from wells; we will walk along the royal road until we pass beyond your boundaries."
verses.21:23: But he was unwilling to grant that Israel pass through his borders; rather, having gathered an army, he went out to meet him in the desert, and came to Jahaz, and fought against him.
verses.21:24: By him he was struck down with the edge of the sword, and his land was taken into possession from Arnon as far as Jabbok and the sons of Ammon, because the boundaries of the Ammonites were held by a strong garrison.
verses.21:25: Therefore Israel took all his cities and lived in the cities of the Amorite, namely, in Heshbon and its villages.
verses.21:26: The city of Heshbon belonged to Sihon, king of the Amorite, who fought against the king of Moab and took all the land that had been under his dominion as far as Arnon.
verses.21:27: Therefore it is said in a proverb, "Come to Heshbon; let the city of Sihon be built and constructed;
verses.21:28: a fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon, and devoured Ar of the Moabites and the inhabitants of the heights of Arnon.
verses.21:29: Woe to you, Moab; you have perished, people of Chemosh. He gave his sons to flight and daughters into captivity to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
verses.21:30: Their yoke perished completely at Heshbon as far as Dibon; weary, they arrived at Nophah, and as far as Medeba."
verses.21:31: Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorite.
verses.21:32: And Moses sent some to scout out Jazer; they captured its villages and took possession of the inhabitants.
verses.21:33: And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came to meet them with all his people to fight at Edrei.
verses.21:34: And the Lord said to Moses, "Do not fear him, because I have delivered him into your hand, and all his people and land; and you will do to him just as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, inhabitant of Heshbon."
verses.21:35: Therefore they struck him down as well, with his sons, and his entire people to utter destruction, and they took possession of his land.
verses.22:1: And they set out and encamped in the plains of Moab, where Jericho is situated across the Jordan.
verses.22:2: Now Balak son of Zippor, seeing everything that Israel had done to the Amorite,
verses.22:3: and that the Moabites had become terrified of him and could not endure his assault,
verses.22:4: said to the elders of Midian, "This people will destroy all who dwell within our borders, just as an ox is accustomed to crop the grass down to the roots." He was king in Moab at that time.
verses.22:5: Therefore he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, a diviner, who lived beside the river of the land of the sons of Ammon, to call him and say, "Look, a people has come out of Egypt that has covered the surface of the earth, settling opposite me.
verses.22:6: Come, therefore, and curse this people, because it is stronger than I am, if perhaps I may be able to strike it and drive it out from my land. For I know that the one whom you bless is blessed, and the one upon whom you heap curses is cursed."
verses.22:7: And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went forth, having the fee for divination in their hands. And when they had come to Balaam and had reported to him all the words of Balak,
verses.22:8: he answered, "Stay here for the night, and I will answer whatever the Lord tells me." While they were staying with Balaam, God came and said to him,
verses.22:9: "What do these men with you want?"
verses.22:10: He answered, "Balak son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, sent to me,
verses.22:11: saying, 'Look, a people that has come out of Egypt has covered the surface of the earth; come and curse it, if perhaps by fighting I may be able to drive it away.'"
verses.22:12: And God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because it is blessed."
verses.22:13: And rising in the morning, he said to the princes, "Go to your land, because the Lord has forbidden me to come with you."
verses.22:14: Returning, the princes said to Balak, "Balaam refused to come with us."
verses.22:15: Again he sent many more, and more noble than those he had sent before.
verses.22:16: When they had come to Balaam, they said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: 'Do not hesitate to come to me;
verses.22:17: I am ready to honor you, and whatever you want I will give to you. Come and curse this people.'"
verses.22:18: Balaam answered, "If Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I will not be able to change the word of the Lord my God, so as to speak either more or less.
verses.22:19: I implore you to stay here tonight as well, so that I may know what the Lord will answer me again."
verses.22:20: Therefore God came to Balaam at night and said to him, "If these men have come to call you, rise and go with them, provided only that you do what I command you."
verses.22:21: Balaam rose in the morning, and having saddled his donkey, he set out with them.
verses.22:22: And God became angry. And the angel of the Lord stood in the road against Balaam, who was riding on the donkey and had two servants with him.
verses.22:23: Seeing the angel standing in the road with a drawn sword, the donkey turned aside from the way and went through the field. And when Balaam was beating her and wanted to bring her back to the path,
verses.22:24: the angel stood in a narrow passage between two stone walls by which vineyards were enclosed.
verses.22:25: Seeing him, the donkey pressed herself against the wall and crushed the rider's foot. But he beat her again.
verses.22:26: And nevertheless, the angel, passing on to a narrow place where she could not turn aside either to the right or to the left, stood directly in the way.
verses.22:27: And when the donkey had seen the angel standing, she collapsed beneath the rider's feet; and he, angry, beat her sides more fiercely with a staff.
verses.22:28: And the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey, and she spoke: "What have I done to you? Why are you striking me now already a third time?"
verses.22:29: Balaam answered, "Because you have deserved it and have mocked me! If only I had a sword, so that I might strike you!"
verses.22:30: The donkey said, "Am I not your animal, on which you have always been accustomed to sit up to the present day? Tell me what similar thing I have ever done to you." And he said, "Never."
verses.22:31: Immediately the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel standing in the road with a drawn sword, and he bowed in homage to him, prone to the ground.
verses.22:32: To him the angel said, "Why are you beating your donkey a third time? I came to oppose you, because your way is perverse and contrary to me.
verses.22:33: And if the donkey had not turned aside from the road, making room for the one standing in opposition, I would have killed you, and she would be alive."
verses.22:34: Balaam said, "I have sinned, not knowing that you were standing against me; and now, if it displeases you that I go, I will return."
verses.22:35: The angel said, "Go with these men, and be careful not to speak anything other than what I command you." Therefore he went with the princes.
verses.22:36: When Balak heard this, he went out to meet him in a town of the Moabites that is situated on the farthest borders of the Arnon.
verses.22:37: And he said to Balaam, "I sent messengers to call you; why did you not come to me immediately? Is it because I am unable to pay a reward for your coming?"
verses.22:38: To him he answered, "Here I am; will I be able to speak anything other than what God puts in my mouth?"
verses.22:39: Therefore they went on together, and came to a city that was on the farthest borders of his kingdom.
verses.22:40: And when Balak had slaughtered oxen and sheep, he sent gifts to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
verses.22:41: Now when morning had come, he led him to the high places of Baal, and he looked upon the outermost part of the people.
verses.23:1: And Balaam said to Balak, "Build for me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and rams of the same number."
verses.23:2: And when he had done according to the word of Balaam, they placed a calf and a ram together upon the altar.
verses.23:3: And Balaam said to Balak, "Stand for a little while beside your burnt offering while I go, if perhaps the Lord will meet me; and whatever He commands, I will speak to you."
verses.23:4: And when he had gone away quickly, God met him. And speaking to Him, Balaam said, "I have raised seven altars, and I have placed a calf and a ram on top."
verses.23:5: Now the Lord put a word in his mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and you will speak these things."
verses.23:6: Returning, he found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, and all the princes of the Moabites;
verses.23:7: and taking up his parable, he said, "From Aram Balak king of the Moabites brought me, from the mountains of the east: 'Come,' he said, 'and curse Jacob; hurry, and denounce Israel.'
verses.23:8: How can I curse the one whom God has not cursed? By what reason can I denounce the one whom the Lord does not denounce?
verses.23:9: From the highest rocks I will see him, and from the hills I will observe him. The people will dwell alone, and will not be counted among the nations.
verses.23:10: Who could count the dust of Jacob, and know the number of the lineage of Israel? May my soul die the death of the righteous, and may my last end become like theirs."
verses.23:11: And Balak said to Balaam, "What is this that you are doing? I called you so that you might curse my enemies, and you, on the contrary, are blessing them."
verses.23:12: To him he answered, "Can I speak anything other than what the Lord commands?"
verses.23:13: Therefore Balak said, "Come with me to another place from which you may see a part of Israel, and may not be able to see the whole; from there, curse him."
verses.23:14: And when he had led him to a high place, upon the summit of Mount Pisgah, Balaam built seven altars, and with a calf and a ram placed on top,
verses.23:15: he said to Balak, "Stand here beside your burnt offering while I go forward to meet Him."
verses.23:16: And when the Lord had met him and had put a word in his mouth, He said, "Return to Balak, and you will speak these things to him."
verses.23:17: Returning, he found him standing beside his burnt offering, and the princes of the Moabites with him. To him Balak said, "What has the Lord spoken?"
verses.23:18: And he, taking up his parable, said, "Stand, Balak, and listen; hear, son of Zippor:
verses.23:19: God is not like a man, that He should lie, nor like a son of man, that He should be changed. Has He said, then, and will He not do it? Has He spoken, and will He not fulfill it?
verses.23:20: I have been brought to bless; I am unable to prevent the blessing.
verses.23:21: There is no idol in Jacob, nor is an image seen in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and the shout of the king's victory is in him.
verses.23:22: God brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like that of a rhinoceros.
verses.23:23: There is no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel; in their own times it will be told to Jacob and to Israel what God has worked.
verses.23:24: Look, the people will rise up like a lioness, and like a lion it will lift itself up; it will not lie down until it devours the prey, and drinks the blood of those killed."
verses.23:25: And Balak said to Balaam, "Neither curse him nor bless him."
verses.23:26: And he said, "Did I not tell you that whatever God commanded me, this I would do?"
verses.23:27: And Balak said to him, "Come, and I will lead you to another place, if perhaps it may please God that from there you curse them."
verses.23:28: And when he had led him onto the summit of Mount Peor, which looks out toward the wilderness,
verses.23:29: Balaam said to him, "Build for me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and rams of the same number."
verses.23:30: Balak did as Balaam had said, and he placed calves and rams upon each altar.
verses.24:1: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he did not go away at all as he had gone before to seek an omen, but directing his face toward the wilderness,
verses.24:2: and lifting his eyes, he saw Israel dwelling in tents according to its tribes. And as the Spirit of God rushed upon him,
verses.24:3: he took up a parable and said, "Balaam son of Beor has spoken, the man whose eye is closed has spoken,
verses.24:4: the hearer of the words of God has spoken, who has gazed upon the vision of the Almighty, who falls down, and thus his eyes are opened:
verses.24:5: How lovely are your tabernacles, Jacob, and your tents, Israel!
verses.24:6: Like wooded valleys, like watered gardens beside rivers, like tabernacles that the Lord has pitched, like cedars near the waters.
verses.24:7: Water will flow from his bucket, and his seed will be in many waters. His king will be removed because of Agag, and his kingdom will be taken away.
verses.24:8: God brought him out of Egypt; his strength is like that of a rhinoceros. They will devour the nations, his enemies, and shatter their bones, and pierce them through with arrows.
verses.24:9: Lying down, he slept like a lion, and like a lioness whom no one will dare to rouse. Whoever blesses you will himself also be blessed; whoever curses will be counted under a curse."
verses.24:10: And Balak became angry with Balaam, and striking his hands together, he said, "I called you to curse my enemies, and on the contrary you have blessed them a third time.
verses.24:11: Return to your place. Indeed, I had resolved to honor you magnificently, but the Lord has deprived you of the appointed honor."
verses.24:12: Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not say to your messengers whom you sent to me,
verses.24:13: 'If Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I will not be able to go beyond the word of the Lord my God to bring forth anything either good or bad from my heart, but whatever the Lord says, this I will speak'?
verses.24:14: Nevertheless, going to my people, I will give counsel as to what your people will do to this people in the last time."
verses.24:15: Therefore, having taken up a parable, he said again, "Balaam son of Beor has spoken, the man whose eye is closed has spoken,
verses.24:16: the hearer of the words of God has spoken, who knows the teaching of the Most High and sees the visions of the Almighty, who, falling down, has his eyes open:
verses.24:17: I will see him, but not now; I will gaze upon him, but not near. A star will rise out of Jacob, and a rod will arise from Israel; it will strike the leaders of Moab and lay waste all the sons of Seth.
verses.24:18: And Idumea will be his possession; the inheritance of Seir will fall to its enemies, while Israel will act mightily.
verses.24:19: From Jacob there will be one who rules and destroys the remnant of the city."
verses.24:20: And when he saw Amalek, taking up a parable, he said, "Amalek is the beginning of the nations, whose end will be destroyed."
verses.24:21: He also saw the Kenite, and having taken up a parable, he said, "Strong indeed is your dwelling place; but if you set your nest in the rock,
verses.24:22: and have been chosen from the lineage of Kain, how long will you be able to remain? For Asshur will capture you."
verses.24:23: And having taken up a parable, he spoke again, "Alas! Who is going to live when God does these things?
verses.24:24: They will come in triremes from Italy; they will overcome the Assyrians and lay waste the Hebrews, and in the end they themselves also will perish."
verses.24:25: And Balaam rose up and returned to his place; Balak also went back by the way he had come.
verses.25:1: Now at that time Israel was staying in Shittim, and the people committed sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab,
verses.25:2: who invited them to their sacrifices. And they ate and worshiped their gods.
verses.25:3: And Israel was initiated into Baal-peor; and the Lord, becoming angry,
verses.25:4: said to Moses, "Take all the chiefs of the people and hang them facing the sun on gallows, so that My fury may be turned away from Israel."
verses.25:5: And Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Let each one kill his neighbors who have been initiated into Baal-peor."
verses.25:6: And look, one of the sons of Israel went in before his brothers to a Midianite prostitute, in the sight of Moses and the entire crowd of the sons of Israel, who were weeping before the doors of the tabernacle.
verses.25:7: When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose up from the midst of the multitude, and seizing a dagger,
verses.25:8: he went in after the Israelite man into the brothel and pierced both of them at once, namely, the man and the woman, in the genital parts. And the plague ceased from the sons of Israel;
verses.25:9: and twenty-four thousand people were killed.
verses.25:10: And the Lord said to Moses,
verses.25:11: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned away My anger from the sons of Israel, because he was moved with My zeal against them, so that I Myself would not destroy the sons of Israel in My zeal.
verses.25:12: Therefore speak to him: 'Look, I give him the peace of My covenant,
verses.25:13: and there will be both for him and for his seed an everlasting covenant of the priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and atoned for the crime of the sons of Israel.'"
verses.25:14: Now the name of the Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a leader from the clan and tribe of Simeon.
verses.25:15: Moreover, the Midianite woman who was put to death at the same time was called Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a most noble chief of the Midianites.
verses.25:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.25:17: "Let the Midianites experience you as enemies, and strike them,
verses.25:18: because they themselves also acted with hostility against you and deceived you with plots through the idol of Peor and Cozbi, daughter of a leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck on the day of the plague for the sacrilege of Peor."
verses.26:1: After the blood of the guilty had been poured out, the Lord spoke to Moses and Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron:
verses.26:2: "Count the entire total of the sons of Israel from twenty years old and above, by their houses and clans, all who are able to go out to war."
verses.26:3: So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho to those who were
verses.26:4: from twenty years old and above, just as the Lord had commanded; and this is their number.
verses.26:5: Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: his son, Hanoch, from whom came the family of the Hanochites; and Pallu, from whom came the family of the Palluites;
verses.26:6: and Hezron, from whom came the family of the Hezronites; and Carmi, from whom came the family of the Carmites.
verses.26:7: These are the families from the lineage of Reuben, whose number was found to be forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
verses.26:8: The son of Pallu was Eliab.
verses.26:9: His sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, leaders of the people, who rose up against Moses and Aaron in the uprising of Korah, when they rebelled against the Lord,
verses.26:10: and the earth, opening its mouth, devoured Korah while very many died, when fire burned up two hundred fifty men. And a great miracle took place,
verses.26:11: that while Korah perished, his sons did not perish.
verses.26:12: The sons of Simeon by their clans: Nemuel, from him came the family of the Nemuelites; Jamin, from him came the family of the Jaminites; Jachin, from him came the family of the Jachinites;
verses.26:13: Zerah, from him came the family of the Zerahites; Shaul, from him came the family of the Shaulites.
verses.26:14: These are the families from the lineage of Simeon, whose entire number was twenty-two thousand two hundred.
verses.26:15: The sons of Gad by their clans: Zephon, from him came the family of the Zephonites; Haggi, from him came the family of the Haggites; Shuni, from him came the family of the Shunites;
verses.26:16: Ozni, from him came the family of the Oznites; Er, from him came the family of the Erites;
verses.26:17: Arod, from him came the family of the Arodites; Ariel, from him came the family of the Arielites.
verses.26:18: These are the families of Gad, whose entire number was forty thousand five hundred.
verses.26:19: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, both of whom died in the land of Canaan.
verses.26:20: And the sons of Judah by their clans were: Shelah, from whom came the family of the Shelahites; Perez, from whom came the family of the Perezites; Zerah, from whom came the family of the Zerahites.
verses.26:21: Furthermore, the sons of Perez: Hezron, from whom came the family of the Hezronites; and Hamul, from whom came the family of the Hamulites.
verses.26:22: These are the families of Judah, whose entire number was seventy-six thousand five hundred.
verses.26:23: The sons of Issachar by their clans: Tola, from whom came the family of the Tolaites; Puah, from whom came the family of the Puahites;
verses.26:24: Jashub, from whom came the family of the Jashubites; Shimron, from whom came the family of the Shimronites.
verses.26:25: These are the clans of Issachar, whose number was sixty-four thousand three hundred.
verses.26:26: The sons of Zebulun by their clans: Sered, from whom came the family of the Seredites; Elon, from whom came the family of the Elonites; Jahleel, from whom came the family of the Jahleelites.
verses.26:27: These are the clans of Zebulun, whose number was sixty thousand five hundred.
verses.26:28: The sons of Joseph by their clans were Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.26:29: From Manasseh was born Machir, from whom came the family of the Machirites. Machir fathered Gilead, from whom came the family of the Gileadites.
verses.26:30: Gilead had sons: Iezer, from whom came the family of the Iezerites; and Helek, from whom came the family of the Helekites;
verses.26:31: and Asriel, from whom came the family of the Asrielites; and Shechem, from whom came the family of the Shechemites;
verses.26:32: and Shemida, from whom came the family of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, from whom came the family of the Hepherites.
verses.26:33: Now Hepher was the father of Zelophehad, who did not have sons, but only daughters; and these are their names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.26:34: These are the families of Manasseh, and their number was fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
verses.26:35: Now the sons of Ephraim by their clans were these: Shuthelah, from whom came the family of the Shuthelahites; Becher, from whom came the family of the Becherites; Tahan, from whom came the family of the Tahanites.
verses.26:36: Furthermore, the son of Shuthelah was Eran, from whom came the family of the Eranites.
verses.26:37: These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim, whose number was thirty-two thousand five hundred.
verses.26:38: These are the sons of Joseph by their families. The sons of Benjamin in their clans: Bela, from whom came the family of the Belaites; Ashbel, from whom came the family of the Ashbelites; Ahiram, from whom came the family of the Ahiramites;
verses.26:39: Shupham, from whom came the family of the Shuphamites; Hupham, from whom came the family of the Huphamites.
verses.26:40: The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman. From Ard came the family of the Ardites; from Naaman came the family of the Naamanites.
verses.26:41: These are the sons of Benjamin by their clans, whose number was forty-five thousand six hundred.
verses.26:42: The sons of Dan by their clans: Shuham, from whom came the family of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan by their families.
verses.26:43: All were Shuhamites, whose number was sixty-four thousand four hundred.
verses.26:44: The sons of Asher by their clans: Imnah, from whom came the family of the Imnites; Ishvi, from whom came the family of the Ishvites; Beriah, from whom came the family of the Beriites.
verses.26:45: The sons of Beriah: Heber, from whom came the family of the Heberites; and Malchiel, from whom came the family of the Malchielites.
verses.26:46: Now the name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
verses.26:47: These are the clans of the sons of Asher, and their number was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
verses.26:48: The sons of Naphtali by their clans: Jahzeel, from whom came the family of the Jahzeelites; Guni, from whom came the family of the Gunites;
verses.26:49: Jezer, from whom came the family of the Jezerites; Shillem, from whom came the family of the Shillemites.
verses.26:50: These are the clans of the sons of Naphtali by their families, whose number was forty-five thousand four hundred.
verses.26:51: This is the total of the sons of Israel who were registered: six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
verses.26:52: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.26:53: "To these the land shall be divided according to the number of names as their possessions.
verses.26:54: To the more numerous you shall give a larger share, and to the fewer a smaller one; to each, just as they have now been registered, a possession shall be handed over,
verses.26:55: provided only that the lot divides the land among the tribes and families.
verses.26:56: Whatever falls by lot, either the more numerous or the fewer shall receive it."
verses.26:57: This also is the number of the sons of Levi by their families: Gershon, from whom came the family of the Gershonites; Kohath, from whom came the family of the Kohathites; Merari, from whom came the family of the Merarites.
verses.26:58: These are the families of Levi: the family of Libni, the family of Hebron, the family of Mahli, the family of Mushi, the family of Korah. Now Kohath fathered Amram,
verses.26:59: who had Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, as his wife, who was born to him in Egypt. She bore sons for her husband Amram: Aaron and Moses, and their sister Miriam.
verses.26:60: From Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, and Eleazar and Ithamar,
verses.26:61: of whom Nadab and Abihu died when they had offered foreign fire in the presence of the Lord.
verses.26:62: And all who were counted were twenty-three thousand of the male sex from one month old and above, because they were not registered among the sons of Israel, nor were they given a possession with the others.
verses.26:63: This is the number of the sons of Israel who were recorded by Moses and Eleazar the priest on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho,
verses.26:64: among whom there was not one of those who had previously been counted by Moses and Aaron in the desert of Sinai,
verses.26:65: for the Lord had foretold that all of them would die in the wilderness. And not one of them remained except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.27:1: Now the daughters of Zelophehad, son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph, approached; their names are Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.27:2: And they stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the people at the entrance of the tabernacle of the covenant, and said:
verses.27:3: "Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the rebellion that was stirred up against the Lord under Korah, but he died in his own sin; he had no male children. Why is his name taken away from his family because he had no son? Give us a possession among the relatives of our father."
verses.27:4: And Moses brought their case to the judgment of the Lord.
verses.27:6: "The daughters of Zelophehad ask for what is just: give them a possession among the relatives of their father, and let them succeed him in the inheritance.
verses.27:7: And to the sons of Israel you shall speak these words:
verses.27:8: 'When a man dies without a son, the inheritance shall pass to his daughter.
verses.27:9: If he has no daughter, he shall have his brothers as successors.
verses.27:10: And if there are no brothers either, you shall give the inheritance to the brothers of his father.
verses.27:11: But if he has no paternal uncles either, the inheritance shall be given to those who are nearest to him.' And this shall be sacred for the sons of Israel by a perpetual law," just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.27:12: The Lord also said to Moses, "Go up onto this mountain of Abarim, and view from there the land that I am about to give to the sons of Israel.
verses.27:13: And when you have seen it, you too will go to your people, just as your brother Aaron went,
verses.27:14: because you offended Me in the wilderness of Zin during the contention of the multitude, and you were not willing to sanctify Me before it over the waters." These are the waters of Contention in Kadesh of the wilderness of Zin.
verses.27:16: "Let the Lord God of the spirits of all flesh provide a man who will be over this multitude,
verses.27:17: and who can go out and come in before them, and lead them out or bring them in, so that the people of the Lord will not be like sheep without a shepherd."
verses.27:18: And the Lord said to him, "Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom the spirit is, and place your hand on him.
verses.27:19: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest and all the multitude,
verses.27:20: and you shall give him instructions while all are watching, and a share of your glory, so that the whole assembly of the sons of Israel may listen to him.
verses.27:21: For him, if anything is to be done, Eleazar the priest will consult the Lord. At his word he himself will go out and come in, and all the sons of Israel with him, and the rest of the multitude."
verses.27:22: Moses did as the Lord had commanded; and when he had taken Joshua, he set him before Eleazar the priest and the whole gathering of the people.
verses.27:23: And after laying his hands on his head, he repeated everything that the Lord had commanded.
verses.28:1: The Lord also said to Moses:
verses.28:2: "Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'Offer My offering, and bread, and a fire offering of a very sweet fragrance at their proper times.
verses.28:3: These are the sacrifices that you must offer: two unblemished year-old lambs daily as a perpetual burnt offering:
verses.28:4: one you shall offer in the morning, and the other toward evening,
verses.28:5: a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour that is mixed with the purest oil and has a fourth part of a hin.
verses.28:6: It is the continual burnt offering that you offered on Mount Sinai, for a very sweet fragrance of a fire offering of the Lord.
verses.28:7: And you shall pour out as a drink offering a fourth part of a hin of wine for each lamb in the sanctuary of the Lord.
verses.28:8: And the other lamb you shall offer likewise toward evening, according to the entire rite of the morning sacrifice and of its drink offerings, an offering of a very sweet fragrance to the Lord.
verses.28:9: And on the Sabbath day you shall offer two unblemished year-old lambs, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice, and the drink offerings,
verses.28:10: which are duly poured out on each Sabbath as a perpetual burnt offering.
verses.28:11: Now on the first days of the months you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs,
verses.28:12: and three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice for each young bull, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each ram,
verses.28:13: and a tenth of a tenth of fine flour with oil as a sacrifice for each lamb; it is a burnt offering of a very sweet fragrance and of a fire offering to the Lord.
verses.28:14: And the drink offerings of wine, which are to be poured out for each victim, shall be these: half a hin for each young bull, a third for a ram, a fourth for a lamb. This shall be the burnt offering through all the months that succeed one another as the year turns.
verses.28:15: A male goat shall also be offered to the Lord for sins, as a perpetual burnt offering with its drink offerings.
verses.28:16: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, there shall be the Passover of the Lord,
verses.28:17: and on the fifteenth day a solemn feast; for seven days they shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.28:18: The first day of these shall be venerable and holy; you shall not do any servile work on it.
verses.28:19: And you shall offer a fire offering, a burnt offering, to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs,
verses.28:20: and the sacrifices of each one from fine flour that is mixed with oil: three-tenths for each young bull, and two-tenths for a ram,
verses.28:21: and a tenth of a tenth for each lamb, that is, for the seven lambs;
verses.28:22: and one male goat for sin, so that atonement may be made for you,
verses.28:23: besides the morning burnt offering, which you shall always offer.
verses.28:24: So you shall do on each day of the seven days as fuel for the fire, and for a very sweet fragrance to the Lord, which will rise from the burnt offering and from the libations of each one.
verses.28:25: The seventh day also shall be most celebrated and holy for you; you shall not do any servile work on it.
verses.28:26: The day of the firstfruits also, when you offer new crops to the Lord, after the weeks have been completed, shall be venerable and holy; you shall not do any servile work on it.
verses.28:27: And you shall offer a burnt offering for a very sweet fragrance to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs,
verses.28:28: and in their sacrifices, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each young bull, two for each ram,
verses.28:29: a tenth of a tenth for each of the lambs, which together are seven lambs; also a male goat,
verses.28:30: which is slaughtered for atonement, besides the perpetual burnt offering and its drink offerings.
verses.28:31: You shall offer them all unblemished, with their libations.'"
verses.29:1: The first day of the seventh month also will be venerable and holy to you. You shall not do any servile work on it, because it is a day of loud blast and of trumpets.
verses.29:2: And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most pleasing aroma to the Lord: one calf from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:3: and in their sacrifices, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each calf, two tenths for the ram,
verses.29:4: one tenth per lamb, which together are seven lambs;
verses.29:5: and a male goat for sin, which is offered for the expiation of the people,
verses.29:6: besides the burnt offering of the first of the month with its sacrifices, and the perpetual burnt offering with the customary libations; with the same ceremonies you shall offer a fire offering for a most pleasing aroma to the Lord.
verses.29:7: The tenth day of this seventh month also will be holy and venerable to you, and you shall afflict your souls; you shall not do any servile work on it.
verses.29:8: And you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord for a most pleasing aroma: one calf from the herd, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:9: and in their sacrifices, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each calf, two tenths for the ram,
verses.29:10: a tenth of a tenth for each lamb, which together are seven lambs;
verses.29:11: and a male goat for sin, apart from those that are customarily offered for trespass as expiation, and the perpetual burnt offering, with their sacrifice and libations.
verses.29:12: Now on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, which will be holy and venerable to you, you shall not do any servile work on it, but you shall celebrate a solemn feast to the Lord for seven days.
verses.29:13: And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen calves from the herd, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:14: and in their libations, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each calf, which together are thirteen calves, and two tenths for one ram, that is, for the two rams together,
verses.29:15: and a tenth of a tenth for each lamb, which together are fourteen lambs;
verses.29:16: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice, and its libation.
verses.29:17: On the second day you shall offer twelve calves from the herd, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:18: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:19: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:20: On the third day you shall offer eleven calves, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:21: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:22: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:23: On the fourth day you shall offer ten calves, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:24: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:25: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:26: On the fifth day you shall offer nine calves, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:27: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:28: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:29: On the sixth day you shall offer eight calves, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:30: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:31: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:32: On the seventh day you shall offer seven calves, and two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:33: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:34: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:35: On the eighth day, which is most celebrated, you shall not do any servile work,
verses.29:36: offering a burnt offering for a most pleasing aroma to the Lord: one calf, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs;
verses.29:37: and you shall duly celebrate the sacrifices and libations of each one, for the calves, and the rams, and the lambs;
verses.29:38: and a male goat for sin, apart from the perpetual burnt offering, and its sacrifice and libation.
verses.29:39: These things you shall offer to the Lord at your solemn feasts, besides vows and voluntary offerings, in burnt offering, in sacrifice, in libation, and in peace offerings.
verses.30:1: And Moses told the sons of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded him.
verses.30:2: And he spoke to the leaders of the tribes of the sons of Israel: "This is the word that the Lord has commanded:
verses.30:3: If any man vows a vow to the Lord, or binds himself by an oath, he shall not make his word void, but shall fulfill everything that he has promised.
verses.30:4: If a woman who is in her father's house and still in her girlhood vows anything and binds herself by an oath, if the father learns of the vow that she has promised, and the oath by which she has obligated her soul, and keeps silent, she will be bound by the vow;
verses.30:5: whatever she has promised and sworn, she shall carry out in deed.
verses.30:6: But if, as soon as he hears, the father objects, both her vows and her oaths will be void, nor will she be held liable to the pledge, because the father objected.
verses.30:7: If she has a husband, and vows something, and a word once going forth from her mouth obligates her soul by an oath,
verses.30:8: on the day the husband hears and does not object, she will be bound by the vow, and shall pay whatever she had promised.
verses.30:9: But if, upon hearing, he immediately objects, and makes her promises void, and the words by which she had bound her soul, the Lord will be merciful to her.
verses.30:10: A widow and a divorced woman shall pay whatever they vow.
verses.30:11: When a wife in her husband's house binds herself by a vow and an oath,
verses.30:12: if the husband hears and keeps silent, and does not object to the pledge, she shall pay whatever she had promised.
verses.30:13: But if he objects at once, she will not be held bound by the promise, because the husband objected, and the Lord will be merciful to her.
verses.30:14: If she vows, and binds herself by an oath to afflict her soul through fasting or abstinence from other things, it will be in the husband's discretion whether she does it or does not do it.
verses.30:15: Now if the husband, upon hearing, keeps silent, and defers his decision to another day, she shall pay whatever she had vowed and promised, because as soon as he heard, he kept silent.
verses.30:16: But if he objects after he has learned of it, he himself will bear her iniquity."
verses.30:17: These are the laws that the Lord established for Moses between a husband and a wife, between a father and a daughter who is still in her girlhood, or who remains in her parent's house.
verses.31:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.31:2: "First avenge the sons of Israel on the Midianites, and so you will be gathered to your people."
verses.31:3: And immediately Moses said, "Arm men from among you for battle, who can exact the vengeance of the Lord on the Midianites.
verses.31:4: Let a thousand men from each tribe be chosen out of Israel to be sent to war."
verses.31:5: And they gave a thousand from each tribe, that is, twelve thousand equipped for battle,
verses.31:6: whom Moses sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest; he also delivered to him the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding a blast.
verses.31:7: And when they had fought against the Midianites and were victorious, they killed all the males,
verses.31:8: and their kings, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, five leaders of the nation; they also put Balaam the son of Beor to death with the sword.
verses.31:9: And they captured their women and little ones, and all the livestock, and all the household goods; whatever they had been able to possess, they pillaged.
verses.31:10: Flame consumed cities as well as villages and strongholds.
verses.31:11: And they took the plunder and everything they had captured, of people as well as of beasts,
verses.31:12: and brought them to Moses and Eleazar the priest, and to the whole multitude of the sons of Israel; but the remaining articles they carried to the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
verses.31:13: Now Moses and Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly, went out to meet them outside the camp.
verses.31:14: And Moses, angry with the leaders of the army, the tribunes, and the centurions who had come from the war,
verses.31:15: said, "Why have you spared the women?
verses.31:16: Are these not the ones who deceived the sons of Israel at the suggestion of Balaam, and made you transgress against the Lord over the sin of Peor, because of which the people were also struck?
verses.31:17: Therefore, put to death all who are of the male sex, even among the little ones, and kill the women who have known men in intercourse;
verses.31:18: but spare for yourselves the girls and all the virgin women,
verses.31:19: and remain outside the camp for seven days. Anyone who has killed a person or touched someone who was killed shall be cleansed on the third and seventh day.
verses.31:20: And of all the plunder, whether it is a garment, or a vessel, or anything prepared as an article of use from goatskins, hair, and wood, it shall be purified."
verses.31:21: Eleazar the priest also spoke in this way to the men of the army who had fought: "This is the precept of the law that the Lord commanded Moses:
verses.31:22: gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin,
verses.31:23: and everything that can pass through the flames shall be purged by fire; but whatever cannot endure the fire shall be sanctified by the water of expiation;
verses.31:24: and you shall wash your garments on the seventh day, and once purified, you shall enter the camp afterward."
verses.31:25: The Lord also said to Moses,
verses.31:26: "Take the sum of what has been captured, from person to livestock, you and Eleazar the priest and the leaders of the people;
verses.31:27: and you shall divide the plunder equally between those who fought and went out to war and all the remaining multitude.
verses.31:28: And you shall set apart a portion for the Lord from those who fought and were in the war, one soul out of five hundred, from people as well as from oxen, donkeys, and sheep,
verses.31:29: and you shall give it to Eleazar the priest, because it is the firstfruits of the Lord.
verses.31:30: Also from the half portion of the sons of Israel, you shall take every fiftieth head of the people, oxen, donkeys, and sheep, of all living creatures, and you shall give them to the Levites who stand guard in the watches of the tabernacle of the Lord."
verses.31:31: And Moses and Eleazar did just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.31:32: Now the plunder that the army had captured was: of sheep, six hundred seventy-five thousand;
verses.31:35: human souls of the female sex who had not known men, thirty-two thousand.
verses.31:36: And the half portion was given to those who had been in the battle: of sheep, three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred;
verses.31:37: from which six hundred seventy-five sheep were reckoned for the Lord's portion;
verses.31:38: and from thirty-six thousand oxen, seventy-two oxen;
verses.31:39: from thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, sixty-one donkeys;
verses.31:40: from sixteen thousand human souls, thirty-two souls fell to the Lord's portion.
verses.31:41: And Moses delivered the number of the firstfruits of the Lord to Eleazar the priest, just as he had been commanded,
verses.31:42: from the half portion of the sons of Israel that he had set apart for those who had been in the battle.
verses.31:43: But from the half portion that had fallen to the remaining multitude, that is, from three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
verses.31:45: and from thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
verses.31:47: Moses took every fiftieth head and gave them to the Levites who stood guard in the tabernacle of the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.31:48: And when the leaders of the army, and the tribunes and centurions, had approached Moses, they said,
verses.31:49: "We, your servants, have counted the number of the fighting men whom we had under our hand, and not even one was missing.
verses.31:50: For this reason we offer among the gifts of the Lord, each of us, what gold we were able to find in the plunder—anklets and armlets, rings and bracelets, and chain necklaces—so that you may pray to the Lord for us."
verses.31:51: And Moses and Eleazar the priest received all the gold in various forms,
verses.31:52: sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels by weight, from the tribunes and centurions.
verses.31:53: For what each one had seized in the plunder was his own.
verses.31:54: And they brought what they had received into the tabernacle of the testimony, as a memorial of the sons of Israel before the Lord.
verses.32:1: Now the sons of Reuben and Gad had many flocks, and they had boundless wealth in cattle. And when they saw that Jazer and Gilead were lands suited for raising animals,
verses.32:2: they came to Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the multitude, and said,
verses.32:3: "Ataroth, and Dibon, and Jazer, and Nimrah, Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Sebam, and Nebo, and Beon,
verses.32:4: the land that the Lord struck down in the sight of the sons of Israel is a very fertile region for pasturing animals; and we, your servants, have very many cattle,
verses.32:5: and we ask, if we have found favor before you, that you give it to us, your servants, as a possession, and not make us cross the Jordan."
verses.32:6: Moses answered them, "Will your brothers go to battle, and will you sit here?
verses.32:7: Why do you undermine the minds of the sons of Israel, so that they do not dare to cross into the place that the Lord is about to give them?
verses.32:8: Did not your fathers act in this way, when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land?
verses.32:9: And when they had come as far as the Valley of the Cluster, after surveying the entire region, they undermined the heart of the sons of Israel, so that they did not enter the territory that the Lord gave them.
verses.32:10: And He, being angry, swore, saying,
verses.32:11: 'Surely these men, who came up out of Egypt from twenty years old and above, will not see the land that I promised under oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they refused to follow Me,
verses.32:12: except Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun; these have fulfilled My will.'
verses.32:13: And the Lord, being angry against Israel, led them around through the desert for forty years, until the entire generation that had done evil in His sight was consumed.
verses.32:14: And look," he said, "you have risen up in place of your fathers, offspring and nurslings of sinful men, to increase the fury of the Lord against Israel.
verses.32:15: And if you refuse to follow Him, He will abandon the people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of the death of them all."
verses.32:16: But they, coming near, said, "We will build folds for sheep and stalls for cattle, and also fortified cities for our little ones;
verses.32:17: but we ourselves, armed and ready, will march to battle ahead of the sons of Israel, until we bring them into their places. Our little ones, and whatever we may have, will be in walled cities, because of the ambushes of the inhabitants.
verses.32:18: We will not return to our houses until the sons of Israel possess their inheritance;
verses.32:19: nor will we seek anything across the Jordan, because we already have our possession on its eastern side."
verses.32:20: Moses said to them, "If you do what you promise, march equipped before the Lord to battle;
verses.32:21: and let every armed fighting man cross the Jordan, until the Lord overthrows His enemies,
verses.32:22: and the entire land is subjected to Him; then you will be blameless before the Lord and before Israel, and you will obtain the regions that you desire before the Lord.
verses.32:23: But if you do not do what you say, no one has any doubt that you sin against God; and know that your sin will seize you.
verses.32:24: Therefore build cities for your little ones, and folds and stalls for sheep and cattle; and fulfill what you have promised."
verses.32:25: And the sons of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "We are your servants; we will do what our lord commands.
verses.32:26: We will leave our little ones, our wives, and our flocks and cattle in the cities of Gilead;
verses.32:27: but we, your servants, will all march equipped to war, just as you speak, lord."
verses.32:28: Therefore Moses commanded Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the families throughout the tribes of Israel, and said to them,
verses.32:29: "If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed for war before the Lord, and the land is subjected to you, give them Gilead as a possession.
verses.32:30: But if they refuse to cross armed with you into the land of Canaan, let them receive places to live among you."
verses.32:31: And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered, "Just as the Lord has spoken to His servants, so we will do;
verses.32:32: we ourselves will march armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and we acknowledge that we have already received a possession across the Jordan."
verses.32:33: And so Moses gave to the sons of Gad and Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and their land with its cities all around.
verses.32:34: So the sons of Gad constructed Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer,
verses.32:35: and Atroth, and Shophan, and Jazer, and Jogbehah,
verses.32:36: and Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for their flocks.
verses.32:37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
verses.32:38: and Nebo, and Baal-meon, with their names changed, and Sibmah as well, giving names to the cities that they constructed.
verses.32:39: Now the sons of Machir the son of Manasseh marched into Gilead and laid it waste, after killing the Amorites who inhabited it.
verses.32:40: Therefore Moses gave the land of Gilead to Machir the son of Manasseh, who lived in it.
verses.32:41: Now Jair the son of Manasseh went and seized its villages, which he called Havvoth-jair, that is, the Villages of Jair.
verses.32:42: Nobah also marched out and captured Kenath with its small villages; and he called it Nobah, after his own name.
verses.33:1: These are the stopping places of the sons of Israel, who departed from Egypt by their companies under the hand of Moses and Aaron,
verses.33:2: which Moses wrote down according to the sites of the camps, which they changed at the command of the Lord.
verses.33:3: Therefore, setting out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover, the sons of Israel, with an uplifted hand, while all the Egyptians were watching
verses.33:4: and burying the firstborn whom the Lord had struck (for He had also executed vengeance upon their gods),
verses.33:6: And from Succoth they came to Etham, which is at the outermost borders of the wilderness.
verses.33:7: Departing from there, they came opposite Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped in front of Migdol.
verses.33:8: And setting out from Pi-hahiroth, they passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness; and walking for three days through the desert of Etham, they camped at Marah.
verses.33:9: And setting out from Marah, they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and there they camped.
verses.33:10: Moreover, departing from there, they pitched tents by the Red Sea. And setting out from the Red Sea,
verses.33:11: they camped in the desert of Sin.
verses.33:12: Departing from there, they came to Dophkah.
verses.33:13: And setting out from Dophkah, they camped at Alush.
verses.33:14: And departing from Alush, they pitched tents at Rephidim, where the people lacked water to drink.
verses.33:15: And setting out from Rephidim, they camped in the desert of Sinai.
verses.33:16: Moreover, departing from the wilderness of Sinai, they came to the Graves of Craving.
verses.33:17: And setting out from the Graves of Craving, they camped at Hazeroth.
verses.33:18: And from Hazeroth they came to Rithmah.
verses.33:19: And setting out from Rithmah, they camped at Rimmon-perez.
verses.33:20: Departing from there, they came to Libnah.
verses.33:21: From Libnah they camped at Rissah.
verses.33:22: And departing from Rissah, they came to Kehelathah.
verses.33:23: Setting out from there, they camped at Mount Shepher.
verses.33:24: Departing from Mount Shepher, they came to Haradah.
verses.33:25: Setting out from there, they camped at Makheloth.
verses.33:26: And setting out from Makheloth, they came to Tahath.
verses.33:27: From Tahath they camped at Terah.
verses.33:28: Departing from there, they pitched tents at Mithkah.
verses.33:29: And from Mithkah they camped at Hashmonah.
verses.33:30: And setting out from Hashmonah, they came to Moseroth.
verses.33:31: And from Moseroth they camped at Bene-jaakan.
verses.33:32: And setting out from Bene-jaakan, they came to Mount Gadgad.
verses.33:33: Setting out from there, they camped at Jotbathah.
verses.33:34: And from Jotbathah they came to Abronah.
verses.33:35: And departing from Abronah, they camped at Ezion-geber.
verses.33:36: Setting out from there, they came to the desert of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
verses.33:37: And departing from Kadesh, they camped at Mount Hor, at the outermost borders of the land of Edom.
verses.33:38: And Aaron the priest went up onto Mount Hor as the Lord commanded; and there he died in the fortieth year of the departure of the sons of Israel from Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month,
verses.33:39: when he was one hundred twenty-three years old.
verses.33:40: And the Canaanite, king of Arad, who lived in the south, heard that the sons of Israel had come into the land of Canaan.
verses.33:41: And setting out from Mount Hor, they camped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:42: Departing from there, they came to Punon.
verses.33:43: And setting out from Punon, they camped at Oboth.
verses.33:44: And from Oboth they came to Iye-abarim, which is on the borders of the Moabites.
verses.33:45: And setting out from Iye-abarim, they pitched tents at Dibon-gad.
verses.33:46: Departing from there, they camped at Almon-diblathaim.
verses.33:47: And departing from Almon-diblathaim, they came to the mountains of Abarim opposite Nebo.
verses.33:48: And setting out from the mountains of Abarim, they passed over to the plains of Moab, by the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
verses.33:49: And there they camped from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in the more level places of the Moabites.
verses.33:50: There the Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.33:51: "Command the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross the Jordan, entering the land of Canaan,
verses.33:52: destroy all the inhabitants of that land; shatter the monuments, and crush the statues, and lay waste all the high places,
verses.33:53: cleansing the land and living in it. For I have given it to you as a possession,
verses.33:54: which you will divide among yourselves by lot. To the more numerous you will give a broader portion, and to the few a narrower one. To each, as the lot falls, so the inheritance will be assigned. By tribes and families the possession will be divided.
verses.33:55: But if you are unwilling to kill the inhabitants of the land, those who remain will be to you like nails in your eyes and spears in your sides, and they will oppose you in the land of your dwelling;
verses.33:56: and whatever I had planned to do to them, I will do to you.'"
verses.34:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:2: "Command the sons of Israel, and you will say to them: 'When you have entered the land of Canaan, and it has fallen to you by lot as a possession, it will be bounded by these borders.
verses.34:3: The southern part will begin from the wilderness of Zin, which is beside Edom, and it will have as its boundaries toward the east the saltiest sea.
verses.34:4: These will go around the southern side by way of the Ascent of the Scorpion, so that they cross over into Senna and reach on the south as far as Kadesh-barnea, from where the borders will go out to the village named Addar and will extend as far as Azmon.
verses.34:5: And the boundary will go in a curve from Azmon as far as the torrent of Egypt, and it will end at the shore of the Great Sea.
verses.34:6: Now the western side will begin from the Great Sea, and it will be closed by that very border.
verses.34:7: Furthermore, for the northern side, the boundaries will begin from the Great Sea, reaching as far as the highest mountain,
verses.34:8: from which they will come into Hamath as far as the boundaries of Zedad;
verses.34:9: and the borders will go as far as Ziphron and the village of Enan. These will be the boundaries in the northern part.
verses.34:10: From there the borders will be marked out toward the eastern side, from the village of Enan as far as Shepham,
verses.34:11: and from Shepham the boundaries will go down to Riblah, opposite the spring Daphnis; from there they will reach toward the east to the Sea of Chinnereth,
verses.34:12: and they will extend as far as the Jordan, and at the last they will be closed by the saltiest sea. You will have this land according to its borders all around.'"
verses.34:13: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying, "This will be the land that you will possess by lot, and that the Lord ordered to be given to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe.
verses.34:14: For the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their families, and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to the number of their clans, and also the half-tribe of Manasseh,
verses.34:15: that is, two and a half tribes, have received their portion across the Jordan opposite Jericho, toward the eastern side."
verses.34:16: And the Lord said to Moses,
verses.34:17: "These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua son of Nun,
verses.34:18: and one chief from each tribe,
verses.34:19: whose names are these. From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
verses.34:20: From the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud.
verses.34:21: From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.
verses.34:22: From the tribe of the sons of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli.
verses.34:23: Of the sons of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod.
verses.34:24: From the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
verses.34:25: From the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
verses.34:26: From the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan.
verses.34:27: From the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
verses.34:28: From the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
verses.34:29: These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to divide the land of Canaan for the sons of Israel.
verses.35:1: The Lord also spoke these things to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho:
verses.35:2: "Command the sons of Israel to give to the Levites from their possessions
verses.35:3: cities to dwell in, and their outlying lands all around, so that they themselves may remain in the towns, and the outlying lands may be for flocks and beasts of burden,
verses.35:4: which will extend outward from the walls of the cities, all around, for a distance of a thousand paces.
verses.35:5: Toward the east there will be two thousand cubits, and toward the south similarly there will be two thousand; toward the sea also, which faces toward the west, there will be the same measurement, and the northern side will end with an equal boundary; and the cities will be in the middle, and the outlying lands outside.
verses.35:6: Now from these very towns that you will give to the Levites, six will be set apart for the aid of fugitives, so that the one who has shed blood may flee to them; and apart from these, forty-two other towns,
